# Agent Instructions
This documentation is published with GitBook. GitBook is the documentation platform designed so that both humans and AI agents can read, navigate, and reason over technical content effectively. Learn more at gitbook.com.

## Querying This Documentation
This site has an agentic ask interface you may use to query the documentation dynamically by asking a question.

Perform an HTTP GET request on the following URL with the `ask` and `goal` query parameters:

```
GET https://developers.oxylabs.io/index.md?ask=<question>&goal=<user_goal>
```

`ask` is the immediate question: it should be specific, self-contained, and written in natural language.
`goal` is what the user is ultimately trying to achieve, the reason they need the answer. Sharing it helps GitBook give you a better, more relevant answer. A goal is most helpful when it describes the outcome the user wants rather than restating the question. For example, with `ask=how do I create an API token`, a goal like `automate deployments from our CI pipeline` lets GitBook tailor the answer to that use case.

The response will contain a direct answer to the question and relevant excerpts and sources from the documentation.

# Introduction

Find everything you need to use Oxylabs’ products effectively, from detailed product documentation to additional resources like the help center, changelog, and more.

Got questions? **Ask our AI assistant.** It’s faster (and way easier) than digging through 1000+ pages of docs.

Just **click the search bar** above and **type your question** – our AI will instantly guide you to the right answer or page.

## Welcome to Oxylabs!

Oxylabs provides tools and infrastructure for accessing publicly available web data. The platform handles the complexity of large-scale web access – **network routing**, **access reliability**, and **blocking resistance**.

## About us

### What Oxylabs helps you do

With Oxylabs, you can reliably retrieve data from websites using your own tools powered by our enterprise-level proxy network or use the all-in-one API solution to start scraping right away without building your own custom infrastructure. Common uses include:

* **Collecting public listings and prices**
* **Monitoring online content**
* **Building datasets for analytics**
* **Powering data-driven applications and AI**

### Who it’s for

Oxylabs solutions are designed for:

* **Developers building data-driven software**
* **Data teams gathering web data at scale**
* **AI teams requiring real-time public data from the web**
* **Companies that depend on unrestricted web access**


# Changelog

Track the latest Oxylabs product updates, feature releases, and improvements. Stay informed on what's new with our tools and documentation.

{% updates format="full" %}
{% update date="2026-10-29" tags="web-api" %}

## Remote MCP server for Web API

Web API now supports a [remote MCP server](/ai-workflows/mcp#web-api), along with the self-hosted MCP Server and REST API. To connect, add `oxylabs-web-api-mcp` to your MCP client’s configuration and authenticate with your Web API credentials.&#x20;

Compatible AI agents and MCP clients can use the Search and Scrape endpoints through a single connection, with no local deployment or server maintenance.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-10-28" tags="web-api" %}

## New parsed output fields for Gemini

[Gemini](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/llms-and-ai/gemini) parsed output now includes `additional_results.sources_results` – a list of every web page Gemini accessed as sources while generating the answer. Send a request to the Web API `/gemini` endpoint with `json` output (parsed), and each entry returns with a `title` and a `URL`.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-10-27" tags="web-api" %}

## Expanded media data collection: TikTok and Bilibili

Web API now supports two new targets under the [media source](/api-reference/dedicated-scrapers/media-scrapers): `tiktok` and `bilibili`, for collecting videos and audios through one API – making it easier to gather media data at scale from one provider.&#x20;

Files are delivered to your cloud storage (S3 or GCS) instead of the API response. The targets use the same workflow as other media targets and accept supported URL formats without pre-cleaning.&#x20;
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-10-26" tags="web-api" %}

## Granular parsed results for ChatGPT shopping

Parsed [ChatGPT](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/llms-and-ai/chatgpt) responses from Web API now include the full product details panel whenever ChatGPT shows shopping results.&#x20;

Along with the existing fields, each product now also includes: `description`, `badge`, `url`, `merchant`, `offers[]`, `citations[]`, `image_page_title`, and `image_page_url`. The new fields are returned automatically. No add-on or extra parameter is needed.&#x20;
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-10-23" tags="agent-browser" %}

## Agent Browser is now on self-service

[Agent Browser](/products/agent-browser/session-inspection-and-recording) is now available on self-service. You can purchase and start it directly from the dashboard – no separate contract is needed.

You can also inspect a session’s activity while it runs, replay completed sessions to review each step the browser took, and save a browser profile to reuse in later runs.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-10-20" tags="proxies" %}

## Geohash targeting with automatic fallback

[Residential Proxies](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#geohash) now support precise location targeting with `geohash`. Add a 1 to 4 character code to the username that covers roughly 39 × 20 km without relying on city or region names.&#x20;

Alternatively, `geohash_fallback` widens the search area by removing one character at a time until an IP is found. If no IP is available in the requested area, the request returns `502`.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-10-07" tags="general-updates" %}

## New Oxylabs Dashboard with credit-based billing

The new Oxylabs Dashboard replaces product-specific subscriptions with credit-based billing. One subscription now covers all Oxylabs products, and usage is charged from a single shared balance.

* **Usage reporting** – view spending and usage in real time across all products, filter by instance, target, and country, and export reports.
* **Instance limits** – set usage-based and monetary limits for each product instance.
* **Top-ups** – add funds to your shared balance from the dashboard.
* **Free credits** – new users receive a **$5 welcome credit** to use on any available product. Unused free credits carry over to the first paid billing cycle only.

Existing users with active subscriptions will be migrated in phases and notified before their account is moved. Learn how to [navigate the new dashboard](https://developers.oxylabs.io/help-center/dashboard/navigating-the-dashboard).
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-10-07" tags="general-updates,web-api" %}

## Introducing Oxylabs Web API

[**Web API**](https://oxylabs.io/products/web-api) is here – search the web and extract what you find, all from one API. The two endpoints share one API key and credit-based billing.

* `/search` returns ranked, location-accurate (titles, descriptions, URLs) in structured JSON format.
* `/scrape` returns page content as markdown, HTML, a screenshot, or structured JSON, with built-in AI parsing.

You can connect Web API to AI agents through [MCP](/ai-workflows/mcp#web-api) or [Agent Skills](/ai-workflows/agent-skills#web-api-agent-skills), without any custom integration. Existing customers have access by default, and new users get $5 welcome credit. Head to the [documentation](/products/web-api) for setup instructions and try both endpoints.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-09-29" tags="proxies" %}

## MASQUE protocol for Residential Proxies

[Residential Proxies](https://oxylabs.io/products/residential-proxy-pool) now support [MASQUE](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/protocols#http-3-masque), enabling modern `QUIC` and `HTTP3` connections through the proxy. This provides more flexible data transport, supporting stable performance and stronger success rates on complex targets.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-08-24" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Granular parsed results for Google Travel: Hotels

`google_travel_hotels` [source](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/search-engines/google/travel-hotels) now returns a more detailed offers field when `parse` is set to `true`, with additional hotel-offer details in every parsed response.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-08-20" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Enhanced parsing for Google search news

Parsed output from the `google_search` [source](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/search-engines/google/search) now returns more detailed data for the additional news component by using `"parse": true` , which appears in searches using the `tbm=nws` parameter.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-08-18" tags="agent-browser" %}

## Improved session consistency for Headless Browser

[Headless Browser](/products/agent-browser) sessions have been improved to stay more consistent while accessing the targeted sites, instead of regenerating it between requests.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-08-17" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Google Books dedicated parser

A dedicated **Google Books parser** is now available through the `google_search` [source](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/search-engines/google/search) using the `tbm=bks` parameter with `parse` set to `true` to receive structured book data in JSON format.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-08-11" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## YouTube Downloader audio parameter

[YouTube Downloader](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/video-and-social-media/youtube/youtube-downloader) now accepts an optional `audio_language` parameter for selecting the audio track:

* `original` – the creator's original audio track
* `default` – the audio track YouTube selects (may be dubbed).
  {% endupdate %}

* [Datacenter Proxies (pay per GB):](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/?route=/overview/datacenter-proxies/buy-now) Finland
* [Datacenter Proxies (pay per IP):](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/?route=/overview/datacenter-proxies/buy-now) Croatia, Finland, Philippines

{% update date="2026-07-27" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Increased prompt limit for Google AI Mode

The maximum prompt length for [Google AI Mode](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/search-engines/google/ai-mode) source requests has increased **from 4,000 to 8,000 characters**.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-24" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Custom browser instructions for LLM sources

[LLM sources](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/llms-and-ai) now support [**custom browser instructions**](/products/web-scraper-api/features/js-rendering-and-browser-control#browser-instructions), allowing you to define actions (e.g., clicks, scrolls, waits) to control page behavior before content is extracted.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-23" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Custom parser for Home Depot data

A **dedicated parser** for Home Depot product pages is now available through the `universal` [scraping source](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/). Enable parsing on your request to receive structured product data (such as `title`, `price`, `availability`, and `specifications`) instead of raw HTML.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-22" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Structured Google Scholar results

[**Google Scholar**](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/search-engines/google/scholar) is now a dedicated parsed source in Web Scraper API. Set source to `google_scholar` and `parse` to `true` to receive parsed JSON directly.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-20" tags="general-updates" %}

## Improved success rates on hard-to-reach targets

We have rolled out improvements to how requests are handled on sites using CAPTCHA. Success rates on these targets should improve, particularly for jobs that previously saw elevated failure or retry rates. Learn more in our [documentation](/products/agent-browser).
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-17" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## More accurate Walmart e-commerce pricing

Parsed output from [Walmart e-commerce sources](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/e-commerce/walmart) now returns pricing data **more reliably and consistently**. If you're tracking competitor prices or monitoring product catalogs, you'll get cleaner numbers automatically with new requests using `"parse": true`.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-16" tags="agent-browser" %}

## Improved fingerprint validation and device-memory alignment

[Headless Browser](/products/agent-browser) now offers more realistic browser fingerprints and continues to align device-memory values with the rest of the emulated fingerprint to lower detection risk for all users. This change applies automatically to all Headless Browser sessions.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-15" tags="general-updates" %}

## Oxylabs Agent Skills

Oxylabs now offers official **Agent Skills** – structured skill files that teach AI agents and coding assistants work with Oxylabs products with significantly more accurate code and fewer hallucinations.

Each Oxylabs agent skill is product-specific and tools like Claude, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot can pick the right product and handle all the technical details with up-to-date information.

Find setup instructions and all skill files in the official [Oxylabs Agent-Skills](https://github.com/oxylabs/agent-skills) repository.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-14" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Citation retries for ChatGPT web search

[ChatGPT source](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/llms-and-ai/chatgpt) requests with `search` set to `true` now retry citation extraction automatically, roughly doubling citation coverage in the parsed `citations` field.

The overall request success rate is unchanged, and no payload changes are needed for requests already using `search: true`.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-07-13" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Batch requests for LLM targets

[LLM sources](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/llms-and-ai) now support **up to 5,000 prompts** within a single batch request for `chatgpt`, `gemini`, and `perplexity` sources. Every prompt runs as its own job, so you get one job ID back per prompt. Learn more about batch requests [here](/products/web-scraper-api/integration-methods/push-pull#batch-query).
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-06-29" tags="general-updates" %}

## Dashboard login: Microsoft Entra SSO

Oxylabs dashboard login now supports **Microsoft Entra ID** (formerly Azure AD) for single sign-on (SSO) in addition to Google and Okta.

To set up Entra SSO, contact your Oxylabs account manager and authenticate the users in your organization to sign in through Entra ID instead of using email and password. Head to [dashboard login page](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/en/) to start.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-06-23" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## New and updated LLM sources for Web Scraper API

Web Scraper API [LLM & AI sources](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/llms-and-ai) now offers a dedicated `gemini` source together with updated `chatgpt` and `perplexity` scrapers. All LLM sources now share a more consistent request structure, streamlined output envelope, and include new response fields (citations, shopping, ads, etc.)
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-06-22" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Partial download (trimming) for Video Data API

[YouTube Downloader](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/video-and-social-media/youtube/youtube-downloader#input-parameter-values) can now download a specific segment of a video instead of the full file by adding `start_at` and `end_at` to the `context` array. Both parameters take an `hh:mm:ss` timestamp format.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-06-19" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Video Data API: video quality selection

[YouTube Downloader](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/video-and-social-media/youtube/youtube-downloader#input-parameter-values) now supports resolution selection for downloaded videos using the `context: video_quality` parameter with specific resolution from `144p` all the way up to `8K`.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-06-18" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Error codes for Video Data API

Web Scraper API `youtube_download` source now returns specific [**error codes**](https://developers.oxylabs.io/api-targets/video-and-social-media/youtube/youtube-downloader#error-codes) in job status response for easier troubleshooting when a video can't be downloaded.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-06-02" tags="general-updates" %}

## Top-up flow improvements

Top-ups for [Residential Proxies](/products/proxies/residential-proxies), [Mobile Proxies](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies), [Datacenter Proxies (per GB)](/products/proxies/datacenter-proxies), [Web Unblocker](/products/web-unblocker), and [Web Scraper API](/products/web-scraper-api) are no longer restricted to fixed values. You can now enter any amount within the range allowed by your plan instead of choosing from a preset list.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-05-28" tags="general-updates" %}

## Oxylabs Dashboard API

[**Dashboard API**](/dashboard/dashboard-api) allows users to programmatically access product usage statistics of Oxylabs [Datacenter Proxies (DC)](/products/proxies/datacenter-proxies) and [Headless Browser (HB)](/products/agent-browser) for automated reporting and real-time usage monitoring without using Oxylabs dashboard directly.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-05-15" tags="proxies" %}

## HTTP/3 protocol support

HTTP/3 protocol is now supported by [Residential](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/protocols) and [Mobile Proxies](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/protocols). Access is available through a dedicated `SOCKS5` endpoint with `UDP` support.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-05-15" tags="proxies" %}

## Session IP change control

[Residential Proxies](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/session-control) and [Mobile Proxies](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/session-control) now support a new sticky session model via `sessid_oneip`, which allows you to keep the same IP for as long as the original exit node remains available up to the set session duration without assigning a new IP after the session expires.
{% endupdate %}

## City and state-level targeting for Headless Browser

You can now set the geo-location of your [Headless Browser](/products/agent-browser) sessions to the city or state level. New parameters include `p_city` for city and `p_state` for state or region targeting.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-03-18" tags="proxies" %}

## Improved proxy upgrade flow

You can now upgrade [Dedicated ISP](https://oxylabs.io/products/dedicated-isp-proxies), [ISP](https://oxylabs.io/products/isp-proxies), [Datacenter (per IP)](https://oxylabs.io/products/datacenter-proxies), and [Dedicated Datacenter Proxy](https://oxylabs.io/products/datacenter-proxies) plans starting from just 5 IPs for ranges between 0 and 100 (previously 20-IP minimum requirement).

The upgrade summary now also provides more details, including discount breakdowns and exact billing dates for easier scaling.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-03-18" tags="undefined,web-scraper-api" %}

## Google Domain parameter no longer available

Web Scraper API `domain` parameter for `google` sources is no longer available. To localize your searches, use the `geo_location` parameter. For more details, check our `geo_location` parameter structures [here](/products/web-scraper-api/features/localization/serp-localization#google).
{% endupdate %}

## Renaming Unblocking Browser

We’re making a change to our product naming: **Unblocking Browser is now** [**Headless Browser**](/products/agent-browser)**.** This is a name change only and all core features, functions, and integrations will remain the same as per pre-existing workflows.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-02-11" tags="proxies" %}

## New ASN providers

IPs from Cox and Deutsche Telekom are now included in [ISP Proxy](/products/proxies/isp-proxies/proxy-list) and [Dedicated ISP Proxy](/products/proxies/dedicated-isp-proxies/self-service/proxy-list) pools. Dedicated ISP Proxy users can choose their preferred premium ASN provider directly from the Oxylabs dashboard.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2026-01-26" tags="proxies" %}

## Dedicated ISP Proxies

[Dedicated ISP Proxies](https://oxylabs.io/products/dedicated-isp-proxies) are now available in the self-service dashboard. This new proxy type provides fully dedicated, static IPs sourced from premium ISP providers and the ability to freely choose your preferred ASNs. Dedicated ISP proxies offer top-tier speed, stable connections, maximum customizability, and unlimited-duration sessions.

Learn more in the [Dedicated ISP Proxies documentation](/products/proxies/dedicated-isp-proxies).
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2025-12-15" tags="proxies" %}

## Advanced filters for Residential Proxies

Residential Proxies support **two advanced filters** that give you more control:

* [**Platform (OS)**](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/advanced-filters#platform-os) – `pl` parameter to select the operating system (e.g., Windows, iOS) of the residential proxy for the TCP connection. This lets you improve your scraping success rates by matching your HTTP and TCP fingerprints.
* [**IP Version**](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/advanced-filters#ip-version) – you can receive only IPv4 or IPv6 addresses from the entire Residential Proxies pool using the `ipversion-4` or `ipversion-6` parameter.

{% hint style="success" %}
To **enable these features**, contact your Account Manager (details available in the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/)). You may need to complete a quick [KYC](https://oxylabs.io/kyc-and-safety) procedure.
{% endhint %}
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2025-12-05" tags="web-scraper-api" %}

## Result Aggregator

Web Scraper API users can now bundle multiple scraping results into large batch files to streamline storage using the [Result Aggregator](/products/web-scraper-api/features/result-processing-and-storage/result-aggregator). Create a custom aggregator via the `/v1/aggregators` endpoint and route jobs to it by adding the `aggregate_name` parameter to your scraping request payloads.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2025-11-25" tags="agent-browser" %}

## Unblocking Browser session inspection

Unblocking Browser now supports real-time visual inspection through a VNC-based [Session Inspection Tool](/products/agent-browser/session-inspection-and-recording#session-inspection-vnc). Add `o_vnc=true` to your connection endpoint (e.g. `wss://user:pass@ubc.oxylabs.io?o_vnc=true`) to open a live graphical view of the headless browser and interact with it directly.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2025-10-30" tags="proxies" %}

## New Datacenter Proxy locations

Five new [Datacenter proxy locations](/products/proxies/datacenter-proxies/select-country) are now available for per-traffic (per GB) users: **Latvia**, **Slovenia**, **Slovakia**, **Greece**, and **Austria**. Requests can now be routed through these countries to optimize coverage and performance.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2025-10-14" tags="proxies" %}

## YouTube Autocomplete scraping source

Web Scraper API can now [retrieve YouTube search term suggestions](https://developers.oxylabs.io/scraping-solutions/web-scraper-api/targets/youtube/youtube-autocomplete) with the new `youtube_autocomplete` source. It allows users to discover related keywords for any search query, which can then be used with the `youtube_search` source to discover more relevant videos.
{% endupdate %}

{% update date="2025-10-08" tags="proxies" %}

## Updated Google Shopping sources

[Google Shopping sources](https://developers.oxylabs.io/scraping-solutions/web-scraper-api/targets/google/shopping) now use the token-based system, replacing the `product_id` workflow. `google_shopping_search` (with `render` enabled) now provides a `token` required for `google_shopping_product` requests.

Additionally, `google_shopping_pricing` is no longer supported as a standalone source. To extract `pricing` data, use the `google_shopping_product` [source](https://developers.oxylabs.io/scraping-solutions/web-scraper-api/targets/google/shopping/shopping-product).

Finally, `google_shopping_product` can now expand the "More Shops" panel to access additional listings by submitting the job with `render: 'html'` (only first expansion is available).
{% endupdate %}

This feature allows Oxylabs to automatically adjust your parser instructions when a parser preset starts to fail due to changes in the target website.

# Quick Start: Web API

Get from an API key to your first Oxylabs Web API search and scrape in just five minutes.

{% hint style="success" %}
Already familiar with the basics? Check out [Web API documentation](/products/web-api).
{% endhint %}

[**Oxylabs Web API**](https://oxylabs.io/products/web-api) gives your application or your AI agent two things the open web makes surprisingly hard: **finding the right, fresh pages, and extracting their data reliably**. One endpoint searches the live web and the other scrapes any page (rendering JavaScript and handling access challenges) and hands back clean data ready for use.

<table><thead><tr><th width="159">Endpoint</th><th>Gives you</th><th>Use it when</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/search"><code>POST /v1/search</code></a></td><td>Ranked results: title, description, URL</td><td>You don't know which page holds the answer</td></tr><tr><td><a href="https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/scrape"><code>POST /v1/scrape</code></a></td><td>One page as Markdown, HTML, JSON or a screenshot</td><td>You know the URL and need what's on it</td></tr></tbody></table>

They are designed to be used together: **search to find, scrape to extract.** This quick start guide covers:

* **Manual integration** – your own code calling the API directly.
* **Easy AI integration** – using the Web API through a proprietary or your custom AI agent.

{% hint style="success" %}
Want to test Web API in a simple UI-based environment before full implementation? Check out [Web API Playground](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/playground).
{% endhint %}

## Setup & API key <a href="#docs-internal-guid-4566d081-7fff-6c77-5105-4c81aa345516" id="docs-internal-guid-4566d081-7fff-6c77-5105-4c81aa345516"></a>

1. **Create an account:** Sign up at the [Oxylabs Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/).
2. **Add a product instance:** Click **+ Add product instance** and select Web API in the Web access category.
3. **Set up:** Choose the instance name, product usage limits (optional), and create the instance.
4. **Get credentials:** Click on the Web API instance in the dashboard home instance table and get your API key.
5. **Export your API key** into your project environment (e.g. your OS terminal or the CLI terminal in the project workspace):

```bash
export OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
```

{% hint style="info" %}
**Note:** Always keep your key server-side. Never commit it to source control or expose it in client-side code.
{% endhint %}

## Web API integration

#### Plugging this into an AI agent?

Skip to [AI agent integrations](#ai-agent-integration) to start using it with one command.

#### Building your own custom integration?

Start the manual integration below.

### Manual integration

Depending on your data needs, you can use the Web API endpoints separately for web search, scraping, or as full data collection and delivery pipeline.

{% stepper %}
{% step %}

#### Search for pages (`/search`)

Find which pages hold the answer to your defined `query`:

```bash
curl https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query": "eu ai act compliance deadlines", "max_results": 3}'
```

<details>

<summary>Output sample</summary>

```json
{
  "state": "done",
  "results": [
    {
      "title": "Implementation Timeline | EU Artificial Intelligence Act",
      "outline": [
        "Date 2 August 2025 Providers: need to be compliant with the AI Act by 2 August 2027..."
      ],
      "url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
      "metadata": { "position": 1 }
    }
  ],
  "params": { "query": "eu ai act compliance deadlines", "location": null, "max_results": 3 },
  "metadata": { "timestamp": 1787431568, "request_id": "1788875675880097469" }
}
```

</details>
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

#### Scrape a page (`/scrape`)

Scrape full page content from any public website by passing the target `url` and the desired output format (`markdown`, `html`, `json`, `screenshot`). Here's a request for page content in Markdown:

```bash
curl https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/scrape \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
       "output": ["markdown"]}'
```

{% endstep %}

{% step %}

#### Full pipeline (search-to-scrape)

`outline` found in `/search` is a list of truncated snippets and often not useful for advanced use cases or AI workflows.

To get structured data from a single query, search the web with `/search` for relevant data according to your `query` and pass the result URL to `/scrape` for data retrieval. Here's a full working Python example:

{% code expandable="true" %}

```python
import os, requests

API = "https://webapi.oxylabs.io"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY']}"}

def research(question: str, read_top: int = 2) -> list[dict]:
    # 1. Discover target URLs
    hits = requests.post(
        f"{API}/v1/search",
        headers=HEADERS,
        json={"query": question, "max_results": 10},
    )
    hits.raise_for_status()
    # 2. Extract full page content as Markdown
    pages = []
    for hit in hits.json()["results"][:read_top]:
        page = requests.post(
            f"{API}/v1/scrape",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json={"url": hit["url"], "output": ["markdown"]},
            timeout=120,
        )
        if not page.ok:
            print(f"skipped {hit['url']}: {page.status_code}")
            continue
        pages.append(
            {
                "url": hit["url"],
                "title": hit["title"],
                "content": page.json()["results"][0]["markdown"],
            }
        )
    return pages

for page in research("eu ai act compliance deadlines"):
    print(f"--- {page['title']} ({page['url']})")
    print(page["content"][:500])
```

{% endcode %}
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

{% hint style="info" %}
**Everything above is realtime – the result comes back in the response.** For high volume data collection we recommend running scrapers as jobs under `/v1/async/scrape` and deliver by polling, callback or straight to your bucket. See [Delivery modes](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/scrape/delivery-modes).
{% endhint %}

### AI agent integration

Oxylabs Web API is designed for easy AI agent workflows using **Agent Skills**, **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) or simple **one-prompt integrations**. Once you have your API key, choose the integration method.

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="One-Prompt Integration" icon="rectangle-terminal" %}
**One-page integration prompt – paste a prompt into a coding agent and have it build a custom integration for you.**

If you want an AI coding assistant (like Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot) to build an integration for you, paste the following prompt:

{% code overflow="wrap" expandable="true" %}

```
Integrate the Oxylabs Web API into this project for live web search and page reading.

Read https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/for-agents.md and follow
it. It has the base URL, auth, both endpoint schemas, reference code, the error and retry
rules, and the checklist to satisfy. If the page does not load, stop and tell me; do not
reconstruct the API from memory.

Decide the path and tell me before writing anything:
- Will this project's own code call the API at runtime? -> write the client the page
  specifies, matching how this codebase already makes outbound HTTP calls.
- Is the web access for you during this session rather than for the project's code?
  -> install the MCP server and the skills, the way the page describes.

The key is in OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY or a .env here. If it is in neither, ask me. Never
print the key: not in code, logs, tests, or your replies to me.

Prove it works before writing tests: make one real search, scrape one URL from the
results, and show me both request ids. If a call returns 401, stop and tell me.

When a scrape comes back empty or skeletal, retry it once with run_js: true. If it is still
empty and the site is on a country TLD (.lt, .es, .co.uk), retry once more with run_js and
location set to that country, then report the page as unreadable.

Then add a test for the retry and error mapping against a mocked transport and run it.
If you cannot run commands in this environment, say so once and give me the exact
commands to run instead.

Report back: the path you took, each checklist item on the page marked done or not,
what I still need to do myself, and anything you could not finish. Do not ask me
whether to proceed; do the work.
```

{% endcode %}

See a full example and learn more about Web API integration in the [documentation](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api).
{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Agent Skills" icon="head-side-gear" %}
**Agent skills – installs the knowledge on how to use the API, no running server required.**

Add official agent skills that teach your AI agent how to search, scrape, cite sources, and handle web research through Oxylabs Web API using the following terminal command:

```bash
npx skills add oxylabs/web-api-skills
```

Now your agent knows all there is to know about Oxylabs Web API and how to use it. To learn more about Web API agent skills, see our [documentation](https://developers.oxylabs.io/ai-workflows/agent-skills).
{% endtab %}

{% tab title="MCP Server" icon="server" %}
**MCP server – typed tools for search, scrape, and dedicated scrapers for any MCP client.**

Connect to or self-host our official MCP server to expose Web API search, scrape, and extract tools directly to Claude Code, Cursor, or your custom AI agent.

For easiest implementation, add the server to your client by pointing your agent to the Oxylabs-hosted server – `https://mcp.oxylabs.io/web-api-mcp`:

<details>

<summary><i class="fa-claude">:claude:</i>  <strong>Claude Code</strong></summary>

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user oxylabs-web-api \
  https://mcp.oxylabs.io/web-api-mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ${OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY}"
```

</details>

<details>

<summary><i class="fa-openai">:openai:</i>  <strong>ChatGPT/Codex</strong></summary>

```bash
codex mcp add oxylabs-web-api \
  --url https://mcp.oxylabs.io/web-api-mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY
```

</details>

<details>

<summary><i class="fa-cursor">:cursor:</i>  <strong>Cursor</strong> (or other clients supporting custom headers)</summary>

For any client that supports remote MCP servers with custom headers, add the server URL and an `Authorization` header to the client's MCP configuration. For example, in Cursor's `mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oxylabs-web-api": {
      "url": "https://mcp.oxylabs.io/web-api-mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Field names can differ between clients – check your client's documentation for how to add a remote MCP server with headers.

</details>

To learn more about Web API MCP integration or how to self-host the official Oxylabs server server, see [MCP servers](https://developers.oxylabs.io/ai-workflows/mcp).
{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

### Essential parameters

#### /search <a href="#docs-internal-guid-5786cd1b-7fff-0a37-d2dd-abcf76c7e3ef" id="docs-internal-guid-5786cd1b-7fff-0a37-d2dd-abcf76c7e3ef"></a>

<table><thead><tr><th width="121">Parameter</th><th width="86">Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>query</code></td><td>string</td><td>Search keyword or phrase</td></tr><tr><td><code>max_results</code></td><td>integer</td><td>Number of organic search results to return (<code>1-20</code>)</td></tr><tr><td><code>location</code></td><td>string</td><td>2-letter country code (e.g., <code>"DE"</code>, <code>"US"</code>) for localized search</td></tr></tbody></table>

#### /scrape

<table><thead><tr><th width="111">Parameter</th><th width="99">Type</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>url</code></td><td>string</td><td>URL to scrape</td></tr><tr><td><code>output</code></td><td>array</td><td>Formats to return: <code>"html"</code> (default), <code>"markdown"</code>, <code>"json"</code>, <code>"screenshot"</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>json</code></td><td>object</td><td>Used for custom AI parsing through prompt or schema</td></tr><tr><td><code>location</code></td><td>string</td><td>2-letter country code (e.g., <code>"DE"</code>, <code>"US"</code>). Some dedicated scrapers use a different format. See <a href="/products/web-api/scrape/dedicated-scrapers">Dedicated Scrapers</a>.</td></tr><tr><td><code>run_js</code></td><td>boolean</td><td>Renders the page in a real browser before capturing content. Slower, use a client timeout of <code>150</code>s or more.</td></tr><tr><td><code>device</code></td><td>string</td><td>Device emulation: <code>"desktop"</code> (default) or <code>"mobile"</code>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

### Common response codes

<table><thead><tr><th width="112">Status</th><th width="322">Meaning</th><th>Retry?</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>200</code> / <code>202</code></td><td>Success. Realtime / async job accepted</td><td>–</td></tr><tr><td><code>400</code></td><td>Malformed request</td><td>No, fix the field named in <code>errors[].pointer</code>.</td></tr><tr><td><code>401</code></td><td>Authentication error (bad or missing API key).</td><td>No, check the key on your Web API instance</td></tr><tr><td><code>429</code></td><td>Rate limit or spent quota</td><td>Rate limit: yes, with backoff. Quota: no.</td></tr><tr><td><code>5xx</code></td><td>Upstream failure or failed to scrape</td><td>Yes, up to ~3 attempts with backoff.</td></tr></tbody></table>

See all [response codes](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/troubleshooting) to learn about all status codes and find troubleshooting tips.

## Next steps

* **Want the full picture of the product?** See the [Web API documentation](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api).
* **Building your first custom requests?** Prototype faster with [Web API Playground](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/playground).
* **Need data from a specific site?** Check out all Web API [Dedicated Scrapers](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/scrape/dedicated-scrapers).
* **Want structured JSON from any page?** Try Web API's built-in [AI Parsing](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/scrape/ai-parsing).
* **Scraping at volume or delivering to cloud storage?** Learn more about available [Delivery Modes](https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/scrape/delivery-modes).
* **Want an AI agent to use the Web API without you writing code?** Try official Oxylabs [MCP server](https://developers.oxylabs.io/ai-workflows/mcp) or [Agent Skills](https://developers.oxylabs.io/ai-workflows/agent-skills).


# Quick Start: Proxies

Start using Oxylabs proxies in just a few minutes with a simple step-by-step guide.

{% hint style="success" %}
Already familiar with the basics? Check out [proxy documentation](/products/proxies) or our handy [Integration hub](/integrations/proxy-integrations).
{% endhint %}

Oxylabs offers a variety of proxy types engineered for high-performance data scraping and improved web access. While use cases for Residential, Datacenter, and ISP proxies differ, the core integration logic is nearly identical.

Follow the step-by-step guide below to start using Oxylabs proxies in just a few minutes:

{% stepper %}
{% step %}

### Setup & credentials

1. **Create an account:** Sign up at the [Oxylabs Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/).
2. **Add a product instance:** Click **+ Add product instance** and select your proxy solution (Residential, Mobile, Datacenter, or ISP proxies)
3. **Set up your proxies:** Choose the proxy type, instance name, (if IP-based type was chosen, [set up your IPs](/dashboard/managing-ip-products#docs-internal-guid-26b69515-7fff-79cb-231a-7643f96de4a1)), authentication settings, and create the the instance.
4. **Get credentials:** Click on your proxy product in the overview instance table and confirm your proxy user credentials.

{% hint style="info" %}
To try our proxies for free, claim a $5 [welcome credit](/dashboard/credit-based-billing#free-credits-welcome-credit).
{% endhint %}
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Your first request

The most efficient way to test your connection is with a cURL command. Copy the template below and replace the placeholders with the values from the **Proxy details** in **Step 3**.

```bash
curl -x ENDPOINT:PORT -U "PREFIX-USERNAME:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Proxy details

Find your specific product below to identify the correct connection details:

<table><thead><tr><th width="172">Proxy type</th><th width="150">Endpoint</th><th width="115">Rotating port</th><th width="125">Username prefix</th><th width="127">Static port</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Residential</td><td><code>pr.oxylabs.io</code></td><td><code>7777</code></td><td><code>customer-</code></td><td>(use <code>sessid-</code>)</td></tr><tr><td>Mobile</td><td><code>pr.oxylabs.io</code></td><td><code>7777</code></td><td><code>customer-</code></td><td>(use <code>sessid-</code>)</td></tr><tr><td>Datacenter</td><td><code>dc.oxylabs.io</code></td><td><code>8000</code></td><td><code>user-</code></td><td><code>8001</code> and up</td></tr><tr><td>Dedicated Datacenter</td><td><code>ddc.oxylabs.io</code></td><td><code>8000</code></td><td><code>user-</code></td><td><code>8001</code> and up</td></tr><tr><td>ISP</td><td><code>isp.oxylabs.io</code></td><td><code>8000</code></td><td><code>user-</code></td><td><code>8001</code> and up</td></tr><tr><td>Dedicated ISP</td><td><code>disp.oxylabs.io</code></td><td><code>8000</code></td><td><code>user-</code></td><td><code>8001</code> and up</td></tr></tbody></table>

{% hint style="success" %}
If you purchased Dedicated Datacenter Proxies (Enterprise) through our Sales Team, you may connect via Direct IP (e.g., `1.2.3.4:60000` for HTTP or `1.2.3.4:1180` for SOCKS5) or use the endpoint provided by your Account Manager. Username requires no prefix.
{% endhint %}
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Customizing your request

Once you have the basic connection working, you can customize your session or geo-targeting:

* **To target a country:**
  * Residential/Mobile: Add `-cc-US` to your username string (adjust the country code accordingly).
  * Shared DC/ISP: Add `-country-US` to your username string (adjust the country code accordingly).
  * Dedicated (DC/ISP): Use the port assigned to an IP in the target country (consult the Proxy List in your dashboard).
* **To keep a static session:**
  * Residential / Mobile proxies: Add `-sessid-qwerty123` to your username string at the end.
  * All Other Types: Change the Port (e.g., use `8001` for IP #1, `8002` for IP #2, etc.).
* **To change protocols:**
  * HTTP / HTTPS / SOCKS5: Change the connection prefix in your client (`http://`, `https://`, or `socks5h://`) following with standard endpoints.
  * HTTP/3 & UDP: Route requests via [MASQUE](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/protocols#http-3) at `masque.oxylabs.io:50000` (Residential proxies only).
    {% endstep %}
    {% endstepper %}

### Next Steps

Now that you've confirmed your connection, here is where to go further:

* **Need advanced features?** See the full feature breakdown for each type in the [Products](/products/proxies) section.
* **Using third-party tools?** Find step-by-step guides for Selenium, Playwright, private browsers, proxy managers, and many more in the [Integrations](/integrations/proxy-integrations) section.
* **HTTP/3 & Native UDP (MASQUE):** If your target endpoints require native HTTP/3 or QUIC connections, refer to the [MASQUE Integration Guide](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/protocols#http-3) for more setup details details.


# Quick Start: Web Unblocker

Start using Oxylabs Web Unblocker in just a few minutes with a simple step-by-step guide.

{% hint style="success" %}
Already familiar with the basics? Check out [Web Unblocker documentation](/products/web-unblocker).
{% endhint %}

Oxylabs [Web Unblocker](https://oxylabs.io/products/web-unblocker) is an AI-powered proxy solution designed to handle the most sophisticated bot traffic management systems (e.g., Akamai, Cloudflare, or DataDome). It automatically manages proxy rotation, browser fingerprinting, and CAPTCHA handling so you can focus on the data.

{% stepper %}
{% step %}

### Setup & credentials

1. **Create an account:** Sign up at the [Oxylabs Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/).
2. **Add a product instance:** Click **+ Add product instance** and select Web Unblocker in the Proxy Solutions category.
3. **Set up:** Choose the instance name, product usage limits (optional), and create the instance.
4. **Get credentials:** Click on Web Unblocker product in the overview instance table and get your credentials.

{% hint style="info" %}
To try our Web Unblocker for free, claim a $5 [welcome credit](/dashboard/credit-based-billing#free-credits-welcome-credit).
{% endhint %}
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Your first request

Web Unblocker is integrated as a proxy. Use the endpoint `unblock.oxylabs.io:60000` and pass your instructions via custom headers.

```bash
curl -k -x unblock.oxylabs.io:60000 -U 'USERNAME:PASSWORD' \
'https://sandbox.oxylabs.io/products' \
-H 'x-oxylabs-geo-location: United States' \
-H 'x-oxylabs-render: html'
```

{% hint style="info" %}
Replace `USERNAME` and `PASSWORD` with your User credentials
{% endhint %}
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

### Essential Headers

Unlike standard proxies, Web Unblocker uses headers to control its AI-driven features:

| Header                    | Value                            | Description                                                    |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `x-oxylabs-geo-location`  | `United States`, `Germany`, etc. | Sets the exit node to a specific country.                      |
| `x-oxylabs-render`        | `html` or `png`                  | Enables JavaScript rendering or returns a screenshot.          |
| `x-oxylabs-session-id`    | `AnyRandomString`                | Keeps the same IP for multiple requests (Sticky Session).      |
| `x-oxylabs-force-headers` | `1`                              | Forces the tool to send your own custom headers to the target. |

### Common response codes

| Code  | Status              | Description                                                  |
| ----- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `200` | `OK`                | Successful request. You receive the full rendered HTML.      |
| `401` | `Unauthorized`      | Invalid API User credentials or missing authentication.      |
| `429` | `Too Many Requests` | You have reached your account's rate limit.                  |
| `550` | `Faulted`           | The system failed to access the site after multiple retries. |

You can find the [full list of response codes](/products/web-unblocker/response-codes) in the Web Unblocker product section.

### Next Steps

* **Advanced browser control:** Need to click buttons or scroll? Check out the [Custom Browser Instructions](/products/web-unblocker/custom-browser-instructions) in the Products section.
* **Geo-targeting:** For localized data, see the [Geo-location](/products/web-unblocker/making-requests/geo-location) page for targeting specific countries, cities, or coordinates.


# Quick Start: Agent Browser

Start using Oxylabs Agent Browser in just a few minutes with a simple step-by-step guide.

{% hint style="success" %}
Already familiar with the basics? Check out the [Agent Browser documentation](/products/agent-browser).
{% endhint %}

Oxylabs [Agent Browser](https://oxylabs.io/products/headless-browser) is a cloud-hosted browser infrastructure that handles bot traffic control systems, CAPTCHAs, and proxy rotation automatically. It is fully compatible with Playwright, Puppeteer, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI applications.

{% stepper %}
{% step %}

### Setup & credentials

1. **Create an account:** Sign up at the [Oxylabs Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/).
2. **Add a product instance:** Click **+ Add product instance** and select Agent Browser in the Browsers category.
3. **Set up:** Choose the instance name, product usage limits (optional), and create the instance.
4. **Get credentials:** Click on the Agent Browser product in the overview instance table and get your credentials.

{% hint style="info" %}
To try our Agent Browser for free, claim a $5 [welcome credit](/dashboard/credit-based-billing#free-credits-welcome-credit).
{% endhint %}
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Your first request

Oxylabs Agent Browser uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). You can connect to it using Playwright or Puppeteer without managing local browser binaries.

**Python + Playwright example:**

1. Install Playwright: `pip install playwright`
2. Run the following script (replace `USERNAME` and `PASSWORD` with your credentials):

```python
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

username = "USERNAME"
password = "PASSWORD"
endpoint = "hb.oxylabs.io"
browser_url = f"wss://{username}:{password}@{endpoint}"

with sync_playwright() as p:
    # Connect to the remote Oxylabs browser
    browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(browser_url)
    page = browser.new_page()
    
    page.goto('https://oxylabs.io/')
    print(f"Page Title: {page.title()}")
    
    browser.close()
```

{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

### Customizing the browser

You can also pass instructions directly through the connection URL using query parameters:

<table><thead><tr><th width="138.5">Parameter</th><th width="172">Example</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>p_cc</code></td><td><code>?p_cc=US</code></td><td>Routes the browser's traffic through a specific country.</td></tr><tr><td><code>p_device</code></td><td><code>?p_device=mobile</code></td><td>Emulates a specific device type.</td></tr><tr><td><code>session_name</code></td><td><code>?session_name=ses-1</code></td><td>Creates a sticky session to keep your remote browser instance running in the cloud.</td></tr></tbody></table>

Find more customization options in Agent Browser [documentation](/products/agent-browser#features).

### Next steps

* **Want to monitor your browser?** Learn about the [Session Inspection Tool](/products/agent-browser/session-inspection-and-recording) to visually track your script's interactions with the browser in real-time.
* **Is your script too slow?** Try [Optimizing Traffic](/products/agent-browser#recommended-setup) to block unnecessary assets from loading. This will increase scraping speed and reduce bandwidth consumption.
* **Encountering errors or timeouts?** Visit the [Troubleshooting Guide](/products/agent-browser/troubleshooting-guide) to resolve common CDP connection issues, library version mismatches, and execution timeouts.
* **Hitting a "403 Forbidden" on a major site?** Check the [Restricted Targets](/products/agent-browser/restricted-targets) list to see which websites or services are restricted from access for the Agent Browser.


# Overview

Oxylabs Dashboard is where you activate products, monitor spending, and manage your account. All in one place to set up and manage as you like.

[Oxylabs Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io) is built around a few core ideas:

* **A credit-based billing model:** One shared balance covers all your products, instead of a separate subscription per product. See [Credit-Based Billing](/dashboard/credit-based-billing).
* **Self-service product activation:** Enable new products directly from the dashboard, instantly. See [Product Instances](/dashboard/product-instances).
* **Real-time spending and usage visibility:** Follow your budget, plan usage, and statistics anytime.
* **Granular instance limits:** Cap spending, results, or traffic per product instance, not just account-wide.

**Want to know all the basics in just 2 minutes? Check the video below:**

{% embed url="<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6piEx4Am77U>" %}

## Overview page

When you log in, the **Overview** page is your home section. It shows:

* Your current plan and real-time spending progress in the top bar.
* A table of all your active product instances.

The top bar shows your current plan and spending budget. For a full breakdown of how this balance works, see [Credit-Based Billing](/dashboard/credit-based-billing).

## Product instances table

{% hint style="info" %}
A product instance is a specific configuration of a service (e.g., Residential Proxies, Web API) with its own name, authentication credentials, and optional spending limit.
{% endhint %}

The Overview page lists all your active instances along with their `Usage`, `Spending`, `Limit`, and `Price`. Use the search bar and filters to find instances by `Product`, `Status`, or `Limit`.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FWPYdzXD3T6tDZC1zJ6Ge%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=9c0c33df-8b0f-483c-b504-b22bf60dc470" alt="" height="312" width="624">

# Product Instances

Learn how to create, configure, and manage product instances in the Oxylabs Dashboard.

A product instance is a specific configuration of a service (e.g., Residential Proxies, Web API) that includes a unique name, authentication credentials, and an optional spending limit.

## Creating a product instance

{% stepper %}
{% step %}

### Start the instance creation

Click **+ Add product instance** from the Overview page. New products can be activated instantly – no account manager or waiting required.

New users are prompted to create their product instance on their first visit:

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FvYj084BtK5Fv5iZFW1Rl%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=92da1c3e-849f-4090-9bb9-1935781ac7e3" alt="" height="315" width="582">

Existing users can find the instance creation option as shown below:

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2F1sUwP5Gxm9XOTNrhb5mP%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=0890503c-a2cf-4f7e-a999-28d595cb7d05" alt="" height="251" width="610">
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Select a product

Choose a product from the list. Products are grouped into categories:

* **Data Collection** (Web API)
* **Proxies & Advanced Proxy Solutions** (Residential, Mobile, Datacenter, ISP Proxies, Web Unblocker)
* **Browsers** (Agent Browser)

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2F1wgtNla3jsDbd68Qh43w%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=c281d677-ca76-4c0d-813d-82ca8f18725d" alt="" height="287" width="610">

{% step %}

### Set instance name and credentials

**Instance name**: Choose a descriptive name.

**Authentication settings:**&#x20;

* **Username & password** (auto-generated, the password can be edited later)
* **Whitelisted IPs** (a list of trusted IPs to authenticate with)

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FNx6nKfC3LCCar43ykuhn%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=4b1886b9-1d4d-4d3f-adbe-7350ea3f1738" alt="" height="413" width="610">
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Configure limits & notifications (optional)

To cap usage on the new instance, set up a limit with:

**Limit type**:

* `USD/EUR` (Monetary)
* `Results`
* `GB` (Traffic)

**Period**: `Daily`, `Weekly`, `Monthly`, or `Lifetime`

{% hint style="info" %}
**Limit type** choice differs by product.
{% endhint %}

Then choose an **Action for exceeded limit**:

* **Disable instance** when the limit is reached.
* **Send email** alerts without disabling the instance.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2F7eH6ntyBgTpEcc0o3KFf%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=821dc630-ef49-4ab2-b92d-abf8599ae691" alt="" height="256" width="610">

{% hint style="info" %}
Instance limits control spending on that specific instance only. They're separate from your overall account credit balance – see [Credit-Based Billing](/dashboard/credit-based-billing) for how the shared balance works.
{% endhint %}
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Finish instance setup

Click **Create instance** to complete the setup.
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

## Managing instances

Click any instance to open its detail page. From there, you can:

* Edit the instance name
* Enable, disable, or delete the instance
* Adjust limits
* View or edit passwords
* Access integration examples
* View usage statistics and the spending limit progress bar

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FmT6Evm1WmGyePNkbZxBg%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=7143d06f-e0c4-44a7-b23c-798acd521df2" alt="" height="525" width="624">

## Granular alerts

Team owner can set spending alerts at the `50%`, `80%`, or `100%` level so you're notified before a product instance or your overall account hits its limit.

{% hint style="info" %}
By default, alerts are set at `80%` and `100%` of your plan limit.
{% endhint %}

Team owner can manage who receives these alerts (recipient email addresses) from the Email notifications settings – see [Team & Account Settings](/dashboard/team-and-account-settings).

## Monitoring spending and usage

### Real-time spending

The top bar on the Overview page shows real-time spending for the current billing cycle.

### Historical data

In the **Spending** tab, view historical data by **Products**, **Instances**, or **Targets**. Switch between `Hourly`, `Daily`, `Weekly`, or `Monthly` views for different granularities.

<img src="https://content.gitbook.com/content/zrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1/blobs/S27WuoQfnJ0ILEceFUvD/unknown.png" alt="" height="329" width="624">

### Usage

The **Usage** tab displays success rates, response time, and other metrics per time interval or target, depending on the chosen product.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FZUfLxeMtJY5vWU1PUC2w%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=fb5a2bf1-a33f-466e-be2f-8afb928729cf" alt="" height="411" width="624">

You can also compare daily usage breakdowns:
