{% hint style="info" %}
To pull usage statistics programmatically instead of viewing them in the dashboard, see the [Dashboard API](/dashboard/dashboard-api).
{% endhint %}


# Credit-Based Billing

Understand how the Oxylabs Dashboard's shared credit balance works across all your products.

With credit-based billing, you purchase a single plan (a recurring subscription for a set dollar amount) that funds one shared credit balance for all Oxylabs products. Instead of a separate subscription per product, you can spend your balance across Residential Proxies, Web API, Datacenter Proxies, and more, all from the same pool.

Credits are deducted according to each product's rates and your actual usage. You can monitor your remaining balance, spending, and usage at any time on the [Overview page](/dashboard/overview) and in the [Product Instances](/dashboard/product-instances) spending and usage tabs.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FBKZ71LsChNtxoONaIMIa%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=936171c4-4792-48bf-b2de-76a47dd664c4" alt="" height="380" width="624">

## Where your credit balance comes from

Your credit balance is **not a pre-funded wallet**. You can't hold a balance without an active subscription. Funds enter your balance only through:

* Your recurring **monthly charge**
* A one-time **Welcome Credit** (see below)
* A **top-up** (see [Upgrading, Downgrading & Top-Ups](/dashboard/upgrading-downgrading-top-ups))

Any unused balance expires when the cycle ends, except where it's carried over as part of an upgrade.

## Free credits (Welcome Credit)

Every new account receives a one-time $5.00 Welcome Credit on registration, added to your balance immediately – no commitment required to start testing products.

* The Welcome Credit applies at the **team level**, not per user (a team of 5 users shares the same $5, not $5 each).
* It's **valid indefinitely** as long as you stay on the free plan.
* If you upgrade to a paid plan, any **unused Welcome Credit** carries over into your new cycle – but only for one upgrade. If your first cycle instead ends normally and auto-renews, any remaining Welcome Credit expires.

{% hint style="info" %}
If you want to test our products at a larger scale than the Welcome Credit allows, [contact our sales team](mailto:enterprise@oxylabs.io) to discuss a tailored trial with the required amount of credits and a timeframe that fits your use case.
{% endhint %}

## Your billing cycle

Your billing cycle is tied to your subscription activation date. For example, if you activate on the 16th, your next payment is due on the 16th of the following month.

{% hint style="info" %}
**Edge case:** If you activated on the 29th, 30th, or 31st, your billing date adjusts to the last valid day of the month (e.g., January 31 → February 28 → March 31).
{% endhint %}

On each billing date:

1. Any unused credit balance from the prior cycle expires.
2. Your full commitment amount is charged.
3. A fresh credit balance is added, and a new cycle begins.

## What happens when your balance runs out

When your credit balance is fully used, the service pauses, there's no overusage allowance in the self-service flow. To keep using the service, you can either:

* **Top up** your balance without changing your recurring plan, or
* **Upgrade** to a higher plan with a bigger budget.

See [Upgrading, Downgrading & Top-Ups](/dashboard/upgrading-downgrading-top-ups) to decide which fits your situation, and how each affects your existing balance.

## Plans

Self-service plans are offered as tiered plans, scaling up to target higher usage needs. You can view current plan tiers and rates directly in the dashboard when selecting or changing a plan.

{% hint style="info" %}
Custom, tailored pricing is also available for larger or more specific needs. [Contact our team](mailto:hello@oxylabs.io) or book a call with an expert to request a quote.
{% endhint %}

## Frequently asked questions

<details>

<summary><strong>How can I test Oxylabs products before paying?</strong></summary>

Every new registration includes a $5 Welcome Credit you can use across any product, with no commitment required.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>What is Oxylabs refund policy?</strong></summary>

Purchases made through self-service are non-refundable. Free credits are provided so you can evaluate our services before purchasing.

</details>


# Upgrading, Downgrading, Top-Ups

Learn how to change your plan or add credits without changing your recurring commitment, and when to choose one over the other.

You can upgrade, downgrade, or top up your plan at any time directly from the [Oxylabs Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io) – no need to contact support.

## Top-ups

A top-up lets you add credits to your balance without changing your plan. Use a top-up when you just need a bit more budget to get through the current cycle, without purchasing a higher plan going forward.

* You can top up **any amount**, at any point during an active billing cycle.
* The amount is charged immediately and added to your credit balance right away.
* Top-up funds **expire at the end of the current billing cycle** – unless you upgrade before the cycle ends (see below), in which case unused top-up funds carry over.

{% hint style="success" %}
**Example:** You're on a $100/month plan, have $20 left in your balance, and top up $50. Your new balance is $70 for the rest of this cycle. If you don't upgrade, that $70 expires when the cycle ends.
{% endhint %}

### **Top-up or upgrade?**&#x20;

Choose a top-up if you only need extra budget for this cycle. Choose an upgrade if you expect to need more budget on an ongoing basis.

## Upgrading your plan

Upgrades **take effect immediately** and you get additional budget to spend right away.

### **What happens when you upgrade**

1. Your current billing cycle ends immediately.
2. Your unused balance (remaining monthly plan’s balance, any top-up funds, and Welcome Credit if you're still in your first cycle) is calculated and preserved as carry-over credit.
3. You're charged the full new plan amount.
4. A new billing cycle starts today, where a `new balance` = `new plan's cost` + `your carry-over credit`.

{% hint style="success" %}
**Example:** You're on a $100 plan with $50 unused. You upgrade to a $450 plan. You pay $450 now, but your new balance is: $450 + $50 = $500, and a new cycle starts today.
{% endhint %}

{% hint style="info" %}
The $5 Welcome Credit only carries over if you upgrade within your **first billing cycle**. If your first cycle ends normally and renews instead, any remaining Welcome Credit expires.
{% endhint %}

## Downgrading your plan

Downgrades are **scheduled** and take effect at the **start of your next billing cycle** – you'll keep your current plan's limits and balance until then.

### **What happens when you downgrade**

1. Your current plan and balance remain fully active until the current cycle ends.
2. On your next billing date, the lower-tier plan amount is charged and applied.
3. Any unused balance from the prior cycle expires as normal. **No carry-over occurs on a downgrade**.

{% hint style="success" %}
**Example:** You're on a $450 plan and request a downgrade to $100 on the 20th. You continue on the $450 plan until your renewal date on the 16th of next month, when the $100 plan and its balance take effect.
{% endhint %}

## Canceling instead of downgrading

If you want to stop using the service altogether rather than move to a lower tier, see [Payment Methods, Invoices & Cancellation](/dashboard/payments-and-invoices).


# Payments & Invoices

Manage your payment methods and billing details, and learn more about invoices and subscription cancellations.

The[ Oxylabs dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/en/registration) allows you to manage your billing information, payment methods, and access invoices from one platform. All payments are processed by our third-party payment providers:

* Card
* PayPal
* Google Pay
* Apple Pay (via Stripe)

{% hint style="success" %}
We never store your card details directly. All checkout and payment-method management happens through your provider's secure, hosted interface.
{% endhint %}

## Managing payment methods

To add, update, or remove a payment method:

1. Go to **Billing & Spending** in the dashboard.
2. Select the **Current plan** tab.
3. Click the **triple-dot** menu.
4. Select **Manage subscription**.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2F8w0BgloLTfFjwuh8xpEu%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=292e13de-8040-4a87-a90d-e768d60bfc5e" alt="" height="244" width="624">

Once you reach the billing portal, you can add a new payment method, set a default, or remove an existing one.

{% hint style="info" %}
`Manage subscription` selection only appears to users with an active subscription plan.
{% endhint %}

### Adding a new payment method <a href="#docs-internal-guid-4f08f6bc-7fff-213f-890f-d8697ca9c68b" id="docs-internal-guid-4f08f6bc-7fff-213f-890f-d8697ca9c68b"></a>

1. In the billing portal, click **+ Add payment method**.
2. A new form will appear with payment options (e.g. Card, PayPal, etc.).
3. Select your preferred method and enter the required information.
4. Click **Add** to save your new payment method. Your new payment method will appear in the list.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FXivyuJh8f1kXSY4KcFrr%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=44f6a6ff-0f4e-42fa-8c07-ede4828bd555" alt="" height="313" width="624">

### Setting a default or removing payment method

In the billing portal, your current default payment method appears at the top of the list. To change it, click the **triple-dot menu** next to another payment method from your list and select **Make default**.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FyNrIKttsWLEfSsK9dhVk%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=10b709ef-c73c-44fc-ac98-36d2acfca0a2" alt="" height="252" width="624">

To remove a payment method from the list, use the same triple-dot menu and select **Delete**.

## Updating billing information

You can edit your billing email, address, phone number, and tax ID from the same billing portal:

1. Go to **Billing & Spending**, select **Current plan**, and click **Manage subscription** in the triple-dot menu on the top right corner of your plan.
2. Locate the **Billing information** section.
3. Click **Update information**, make your changes, and save.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FL9Uv5eD7vQErzBOMfe58%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=070fc6b7-458f-4a51-ae48-58b0e03c87e4" alt="" height="312" width="624">

## Canceling your subscription

1. In your billing portal, click **Cancel subscription** in the top-right corner.
2. Confirm your cancellation when prompted.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2Fji9s4KrpanPjVGYSmeKe%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=c51ab56f-d625-4859-b450-a2b2eccabca5" alt="" height="311" width="624">

{% hint style="info" %}
Cancellation takes effect at the end of your current billing cycle. You keep full access to the service and your remaining credit balance until then. Any unused balance at the end of the final cycle expires, and no refunds are issued for unused balance.
{% endhint %}

If your subscription is already inactive, you'll see a **Resubscribe** option in place of Cancel subscription.

## Receipts and invoices

You can view and download your invoices from **Billing & Spending** section's **Invoices** tab.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FLbx4z0krKuSg0GrFuEvx%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=b9cd8d9c-747d-4be0-8ae0-26c6a54143eb" alt="" height="180" width="624">

Your account generates two types of financial documents:

<table><thead><tr><th width="153.5">Document</th><th>When it's generated</th><th>What it means</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Payment Receipt</strong></td><td>Immediately after any successful payment (subscription activation, renewal, or top-up)</td><td>Confirms funds were received and credit was added. Not a legal/tax document.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Final Invoice</strong></td><td>At the end of each billing cycle</td><td>Your official Tax Invoice, marked <strong>Paid in Full</strong>, detailing how your commitment was used that cycle.</td></tr></tbody></table>

## If a payment fails

If your recurring charge fails on your billing date, you enter a **7-day grace period**:

* Your subscription and usage remain active, but your remaining balance is capped at 25% usage during this window.
* Payment retries are handled automatically at optimized intervals – no action is needed on your end while retries are in progress.
* You can still **upgrade** during the grace period, but you can't top up.

Your service is suspended if either of the following happens first: the 7-day grace period ends without a successful payment, or your balance reaches $0.

{% hint style="warning" %}
If your service is suspended due to a failed payment, any assigned IPs are released. Your instance configurations are preserved, but you'll need to re-add IPs after reactivating. You may receive different IPs than before.

To reactivate, purchase a new plan. A new billing cycle starts on the reactivation date.
{% endhint %}


# Team & Account Settings

Manage your team members, account settings, and notification preferences in the Oxylabs Dashboard.

The **Settings** section is accessible from the Overview page and includes **Settings**, **Team**, and **Email notifications**.

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FRE6DZGKjRX2ENZQO3t2y%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=99b98ea6-f6f3-4430-bc16-b4a2473df229" alt="" height="396" width="624">

From here you can:

* Change your password
* Select your region
* Manage team members
* Configure email notifications

## Team roles

Oxylabs Teams consist of two roles:

* **Team owner** – Manages the team, invites members, and controls subscriptions.
* **Team member** – Has access to dashboard features but cannot manage subscriptions or invite other members.

#### **Team member restrictions:**

* Only the team owner can add new members.
* Maximum of `50` active team members.
* Team members purchase subscriptions.
* A user with **Free plan** who joins a team loses their plan and gains access to the team's dashboard and products instead.
* A user with an active subscription must cancel it (under **Billing & Spending**) before joining a team.
* A user can belong to only one team at a time. To create a new team, they must first leave their current one.

## Inviting team members

1. Go to **Settings → Team**.
2. Click **+ Invite team member**.
3. Enter the teammate's email address and send the invitation.

![](https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FNBTmMH1AgZxWnO6lKffu%2FScreenshot%202026-09-16%20at%2010.58.00.png?alt=media\&token=75bc3092-2fd6-45c6-a7eb-690b933fd43a)

The invitee receives an email invitation and, if they already have an account, a dashboard notification too. Once they accept, their status changes to **Active**. You can resend invitations or remove team members at any time.

### Team member onboarding

1. The invitee receives an email invitation.
2. Clicking **Accept invitation** takes them to the dashboard – they'll need to register first if they don't already have an account.
3. Once accepted, they get access to all dashboard features except subscription management and team invitations.
4. They can view their membership details, or leave the team at any time, under **Settings** → **Team**.

### Transferring team ownership

1. The current owner selects a new owner from the existing team.
2. They confirm the transfer in the dashboard and via email verification.
3. The new owner accepts via the dashboard or email.

Once complete, the new owner has full administrative control, and the previous owner becomes a regular team member.

## Email notifications

The email notification settings let you configure account-level alerts, plus the email addresses that should receive them. **Spending limit notifications** notify you as you approach and reach your overall monthly spending limit (e.g., at `50%`, `80%`, or `100%`).

<img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2Fg3wMFNh7OAimF6vILRye%2Funknown.png?alt=media&amp;token=d85132fe-8916-43b7-ad35-7eb69f634108" alt="" height="344" width="624">

{% hint style="info" %}
By default, `80%` and `100%` spending alerts are set. See [Product Instances](/dashboard/product-instances) for instance-level alert configuration (separate from these account-level alerts).
{% endhint %}

## Account verification

Oxylabs may require account verification as part of compliance and platform-security processes. If verification is needed, the team owner receives instructions in the dashboard for submitting the requested information.


# Managing IP Products

Learn how to manage your IPs, understand per-IP billing, and see what happens to your proxy list when your plan changes.

Pay-per-IP products can be managed in the dashboard:

* Datacenter Proxies
* Dedicated Datacenter Proxies
* ISP Proxies
* Dedicated ISP Proxies

## Acquiring IP products <a href="#docs-internal-guid-26b69515-7fff-79cb-231a-7643f96de4a1" id="docs-internal-guid-26b69515-7fff-79cb-231a-7643f96de4a1"></a>

Start by clicking **+ Add product instance** and select an IP-based product. Then choose **Pay per IP** option and the **number of IPs** for the product instance.

![](https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FKby8ccqM6nPI1iv26jgq%2Funknown.png?alt=media\&token=0efca66d-fd14-4aa6-ab95-0964e3cae040)

Finally, **set up the IP locations** and choose the number for each location.&#x20;

{% hint style="success" %}
Continuing with no chosen locations will assign IPs randomly.
{% endhint %}

![](https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FDP5m5cY2vrt3pxgPsYvd%2Funknown.png?alt=media\&token=4b6b3c47-8c33-4aae-ae52-2ff25f7411a0)

## Managing IPs

Navigate to the relevant instance and select **Proxy list** to manage your proxies.

![](https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FBgVfCGmum6TZe5ZVgyX6%2FScreenshot%202026-09-16%20at%2011.07.03.png?alt=media\&token=da59a575-6e70-442b-9aa1-788447649de1)

From the proxy list, you can:

* **Add/modify** – add new proxies or update IP locations of existing ones.
* **Refresh** – replace selected proxy IPs with new ones.
* **Remove** – delete selected proxies.

{% hint style="warning" %}
Updating the locations of existing proxies through **Add/modify** is free. Using **Refresh** applies a one-time fee (billed per IP)
{% endhint %}

<figure><img src="https://63892162-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FzrXw45naRpCZ0Ku9AjY1%2Fuploads%2FYUnQb2cBpgrscBeLUKhN%2FScreenshot%202026-09-16%20at%2011.10.22.png?alt=media&amp;token=622a29a0-d732-4220-90c7-8db850ca8f22" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>

{% hint style="info" %}
For any changes to Enterprise Dedicated Datacenter Proxies, [contact support](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) or your dedicated account manager.
{% endhint %}

## IP product billing

Pay-per-IP products (Datacenter Proxies, ISP Proxies, Dedicated Datacenter Proxies, Dedicated ISP Proxies) are billed **daily**. The daily charge is calculated by dividing the total monthly cost by 30 days, regardless of the calendar month.

{% hint style="success" %}
**Example:** A monthly IP cost of $300 equates to a daily charge of $10 ($300 ÷ 30 days).
{% endhint %}

{% hint style="info" %}
Enterprise Dedicated Datacenter Proxies are billed monthly instead.
{% endhint %}

## Proxy list changes on upgrade, downgrade, or renewal

For details on how your assigned IPs are affected when you upgrade, downgrade, or renew your plan, see the [IP Replacement](/products/proxies/ip-replacement) page.


# Dashboard API

Programmatic access to Oxylabs product users for tracking usage statistics with the Dashboard API.

The **Dashboard API** allows you to **access your product usage statistics** programmatically and integrate the metrics into your internal systems. This allows automated reporting and real-time usage monitoring without using the Oxylabs dashboard on the web.

{% hint style="info" %}
**Note:** Dashboard API currently supports **Datacenter Proxies (DC**) and **Agent Browser (HB)**. You can also track [**Residential Proxies**](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/public-api), [**Mobile Proxies**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/public-api), [**Web Unblocker**](/products/web-unblocker/usage-statistics), and [**Web Scraper API**](/products/web-scraper-api/usage-and-billing/usage-statistics) usage statistics with simple API requests.
{% endhint %}

All API requests flow through this base path:

```
https://api.oxylabs.io/
```

## Authentication

{% hint style="warning" %}
**Important:** To get your Dashboard API key, please contact our [**Customer Support**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) team. Once requested, the key will be generated and given to you directly within one business day.
{% endhint %}

You must include the key in the `Authorization` header of every request using the `Bearer` scheme.

```
Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_API_KEY}
```

## Endpoints

Dashboard API includes endpoints for product Instance Discovery and Usage Statistics. All responses are delivered in JSON format.

<table><thead><tr><th width="236.8125">Endpoint</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="#instance-discovery">Instance discovery</a></td><td>The request returns a paginated list of product instances your account is authorized to access. You can use the returned IDs to filter results when calling other endpoints.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="#usage-statistics">Usage statistics</a></td><td>The request returns aggregated usage statistics per product for the authenticated client's product instances.</td></tr></tbody></table>

### Instance Discovery

```
GET /stats/v1/filters/instances
```

#### Query parameters

<table><thead><tr><th width="166">Parameter</th><th width="268.0481770833333">Description</th><th>Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>products[]</code></td><td>Filter by product. Accepted values: <code>HB</code> (Agent Browser), <code>DC</code> (Datacenter Proxies), <code>null</code> (all products).</td><td>Array of strings</td></tr><tr><td><code>page</code></td><td>Page number. Default: <code>1</code>.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>per_page</code></td><td>Results per page. Default: <code>100</code>. Maximum: <code>100</code>.</td><td>Integer</td></tr></tbody></table>

#### Example request

To start filtering data, you first need to identify your specific resources. The following example shows how to list your available Datacenter Proxies (DC) and Agent Browser (HB) instances.

**Input sample**

```
GET /stats/v1/filters/instances?products[]=HB&products[]=DC&page=1&per_page=50
Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_API_KEY}
```

**Output sample**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "uuid": "my-hb-instance-uuid",
      "name": "my-hb-instance",
      "status": "enabled",
      "product": "HB"
    },
    {
      "uuid": "my-dc-instance-uuid",
      "name": "my-dc-instance",
      "status": "disabled",
      "product": "DC"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "per_page": 50,
      "total_items": 2,
      "total_pages": 1
    }
  }
}
```

#### Response fields

<table><thead><tr><th width="166">Field</th><th width="268.0481770833333">Description</th><th>Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>uuid</code></td><td>Unique identifier for the instance.</td><td>String (UUID)</td></tr><tr><td><code>name</code></td><td>Instance name as configured in the dashboard.</td><td>String</td></tr><tr><td><code>status</code></td><td>Product instance status (e.g., <code>enabled</code> or <code>disabled</code>).</td><td>String</td></tr><tr><td><code>product</code></td><td>Product identifier (e.g., <code>HB</code> (Agent Browser), <code>DC</code> (Datacenter Proxies), etc.).</td><td>String</td></tr><tr><td><code>page</code></td><td>Current page number.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>per_page</code></td><td>Number of results on this page.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>total_items</code></td><td>Total matching records across all pages.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>total_pages</code></td><td>Total number of pages. Always at least <code>1</code>, even when there are no results.</td><td>Integer</td></tr></tbody></table>

### Usage Statistics

```
GET /stats/v1/usage
```

{% hint style="warning" %}
**Important:** The maximum date range for a single request (the difference between `date_to` and `date_from`) is **31 days**. To retrieve usage data for a longer period, please perform your queries in 31-day batches.
{% endhint %}

#### Query parameters

<table><thead><tr><th width="166">Parameter</th><th width="268.0481770833333">Description</th><th>Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><mark style="background-color:green;"><code>product</code></mark></td><td>Product identifier (e.g., <code>HB</code> (Agent Browser), <code>DC</code> (Datacenter Proxies), etc.)</td><td>String</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="background-color:green;"><code>date_to</code></mark></td><td>Start date, inclusive (e.g., UTC <code>YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ</code> or offset-aware <code>YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss+02:00</code>).</td><td>Date (ISO 8601)</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="background-color:green;"><code>date_from</code></mark></td><td>End date, inclusive. Same format as <code>date_to</code>.</td><td>Date (ISO 8601)</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="background-color:green;"><code>group_by</code></mark></td><td>Result grouping options. Accepted values: <code>DAY</code>, <code>TARGET</code>, <code>INSTANCE</code>. Multiple values can be combined. The order of values determines the order of data grouping.</td><td>Array of strings</td></tr><tr><td><code>instances[]</code></td><td>Filter results to specific instances. Accepts multiple UUIDs obtained from <code>GET /stats/v1/filters/instances</code>. Invalid or unrecognized UUIDs are ignored.</td><td>UUID (Array of strings)</td></tr><tr><td><code>page</code></td><td>Page number. Default: <code>1</code>.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>per_page</code></td><td>Results per page. Default: <code>100</code>. Maximum: <code>100</code>.</td><td>Integer</td></tr></tbody></table>

\- mandatory parameter

#### Example requests

**1. Group by TARGET**

The following example shows how to retrieve usage metrics for Agent Browser (`HB`) by grouping results by target, to see the total request count and traffic volume for each target within the selected date range.

**Input sample**

```
GET /stats/v1/usage?product=HB&date_from=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z&date_to=2025-11-30T23:59:59Z&group_by[]=TARGET
Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_API_KEY}
```

**Output sample**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {"grouped_by": ["some.target.A"], "requests": 10, "traffic_bytes": 100},
    {"grouped_by": ["some.target.B"], "requests": 10, "traffic_bytes": 100}
  ],
  "totals": {
    "requests": 20,
    "traffic_bytes": 200
  },
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "per_page": 50,
      "total_items": 100,
      "total_pages": 2
    },
    "grouping": ["TARGET"]
  }
```

**2. Group by DAY + TARGET**

This example shows how to break down Agent Browser (`HB`) usage by both `Day` and `Target` to see exactly how much traffic each target consumed on a day-by-day basis.

**Input sample**

```
GET /stats/v1/usage?product=HB&date_from=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z&date_to=2025-11-30T23:59:59Z&group_by[]=DAY&group_by[]=TARGET
Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_API_KEY}
```

**Output sample**

```json

  "data": [
    {"grouped_by": ["2025-11-01", "some.target.A"], "requests": 10, "traffic_bytes": 100},
    {"grouped_by": ["2025-11-01", "some.target.B"], "requests": 10, "traffic_bytes": 100},
    {"grouped_by": ["2025-11-02", "some.target.A"], "requests": 10, "traffic_bytes": 100},
    {"grouped_by": ["2025-11-02", "some.target.B"], "requests": 10, "traffic_bytes": 100}
  ],
  "totals": {
    "requests": 40,
    "traffic_bytes": 400
  },
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "per_page": 50,
      "total_items": 200,
      "total_pages": 4
    },
    "grouping": ["DAY", "TARGET"]
  }
}
```

#### Response fields

<table><thead><tr><th width="190">Field</th><th width="344.0481770833333">Description</th><th>Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>grouped_by</code></td><td>Grouping options in the same order as the requested <code>group_by</code> parameters.</td><td>Array of strings</td></tr><tr><td><code>data.requests</code></td><td>Total request count for the grouped period/dimension combination.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>data.traffic_bytes</code></td><td>Total traffic in bytes for the grouped period/dimension combination.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>totals</code></td><td>Total aggregated values for the selected period.</td><td>Object</td></tr><tr><td><code>totals.requests</code></td><td>Total request count across the entire selected period.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>totals.traffic_bytes</code></td><td>Total traffic in bytes across the entire selected period.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>page</code></td><td>Current page number.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>per_page</code></td><td>Number of results on this page.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>total_items</code></td><td>Total matching records across all pages.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>total_pages</code></td><td>Total number of pages. Always at least <code>1</code>, even when there are no results.</td><td>Integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>meta.grouping</code></td><td>The active grouping options in the order they appear in <code>grouped_by</code>. Mirrors the <code>group_by</code> request parameter.</td><td>Array of strings</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Rate Limits

To ensure stability, Dashboard API rate limits are applied per API key and per client account for all requests.

* `10` requests per API key
* `100` requests across all API keys of an individual client

## Error Handling

Here are some common error types that you can get while using the Dashboard API:

<table><thead><tr><th width="166">Error code</th><th width="268.0481770833333">Error message</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>400</code></td><td>Bad request</td><td>The request could not be understood. Please check if the request is formatted correctly.</td></tr><tr><td><code>401</code></td><td>Invalid request</td><td>User has entered an invalid API key.</td></tr><tr><td><code>403</code></td><td>Forbidden</td><td>Access denied: missing API key. Please contact support or your account manager.</td></tr><tr><td><code>429</code></td><td>Too many requests</td><td>User has reached the thread/concurrent session limit.</td></tr><tr><td><code>500</code></td><td>Internal server error</td><td>We had an unexpected problem with the server. Try again later.</td></tr></tbody></table>

For questions, access issues, or integration support, please contact [**support@oxylabs.io**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) or your account manager. When reporting a problem, please include:

* The endpoint and query parameters used
* The HTTP status code returned
* The full response body (redact your API key before sharing)
* Timestamps of the failing requests (UTC preferred)

# Web API

Learn how to use and integrate Oxylabs Web API – an all-in-one REST API for web search and page data collection.

The Oxylabs Web API gives applications and AI agents live access to the open web through a unified REST interface. It handles JavaScript rendering, bot traffic challenges, proxy rotation, and geo-targeting through separate endpoint for different web data acquisition stages:

<table><thead><tr><th width="106">Endpoint</th><th width="504">Used for</th><th width="148">Input</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="/products/web-api/search">/search</a></td><td>Discovering and ranking organic web results.</td><td>Keyword / Query</td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/web-api/scrape">/scrape</a></td><td>Rendering and extracting page data as Markdown, HTML, JSON, or Screenshot.</td><td>Page URL</td></tr></tbody></table>

{% hint style="success" %}
Web API endpoints are designed to be used together: **search to find, scrape to read.** `/search` descriptions are snippets, so anything you need to be accurate about comes from a `/scrape`.
{% endhint %}

## How to use it

### Get an API key

In the [Oxylabs dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io), create a **Web API** instance, get the API key from the product instance, and export it to your project environment (e.g. your OS terminal or the CLI terminal in the project workspace):

```bash
export OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
```

See [Authentication](/products/web-api/authentication) for key handling and rotation.

### Choose integration method

* **Plugging this into an AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, or your own agent)?**\
  Check the [AI agent integrations](#ai-agent-integration) to start using it with one command.
* **Building your own integration?**\
  Follow the steps below to integrate directly using REST endpoints.

### Manual integration

{% stepper %}
{% step %}

#### Search

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```bash
curl https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query": "eu ai act compliance deadlines", "max_results": 3}'
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import os, requests

resp = requests.post(
    "https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/search",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"query": "eu ai act compliance deadlines", "max_results": 3},
    timeout=120,
)
resp.raise_for_status()

for r in resp.json()["results"]:
    print(r["metadata"]["position"], r["title"], r["url"], sep=" | ")
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Node.js" %}

```javascript
const res = await fetch("https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/search", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ query: "eu ai act compliance deadlines", max_results: 3 }),
});
if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${res.status} ${await res.text()}`);

const { results } = await res.json();
results.forEach((r) => console.log(r.metadata.position, r.title, r.url));
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

**Output sample**

```json
{
  "state": "done",
  "results": [
    {
      "title": "Implementation Timeline | EU Artificial Intelligence Act",
      "outline": [
        "Date 2 August 2025 Providers: need to be compliant with the AI Act by 2 August 2027..."
      ],
      "url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
      "metadata": { "position": 1 }
    }
  ],
  "params": { "query": "eu ai act compliance deadlines", "location": null, "max_results": 3 },
  "metadata": { "timestamp": 1787431568, "request_id": "1788875675880097469" }
}
```

See [/search](/products/web-api/search) for request parameters and output dictionary.
{% endstep %}

#### Scrape

Read the pages collected by `/search` or your URL list:

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```bash
curl https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/scrape \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
      "url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
      "output": ["markdown"]
  }'
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
page = requests.post(
    "https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/scrape",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
        "output": ["markdown"],
    },
    timeout=120,
)
page.raise_for_status()
print(page.json()["results"][0]["markdown"][:2000])
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Node.js" %}

```javascript
const page = await fetch("https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/scrape", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    url: "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
    output: ["markdown"],
  }),
});
if (!page.ok) throw new Error(`${page.status} ${await page.text()}`);

const { results } = await page.json();
console.log(results[0].markdown.slice(0, 2000));
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

See [/scrape](/products/web-api/scrape) for request parameters, output dictionary, delivery modes .
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

#### Combine: search-to-scrape

Search snippets (`outline`) are truncated and insufficient for deep analysis or LLM pipelines. The standard integration pattern queries `/v1/search` to discover authoritative links, then routes those URLs to `/v1/scrape` requesting Markdown output to strip unnecessary HTML artifacts.

Python example below shows both endpoints in a single workflow:

{% code expandable="true" %}

```python
import os, requests

API = "https://webapi.oxylabs.io"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY']}"}


def research(question: str, read_top: int = 2) -> list[dict]:
    # 1. Discover target URLs
    hits = requests.post(
        f"{API}/v1/search",
        headers=HEADERS,
        json={"query": question, "max_results": 10},
        timeout=120,
    )
    hits.raise_for_status()
    # 2. Extract full page content as Markdown
    pages = []
    for hit in hits.json()["results"][:read_top]:
        page = requests.post(
            f"{API}/v1/scrape",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json={"url": hit["url"], "output": ["markdown"]},
            timeout=120,
        )
        if not page.ok:
            print(f"skipped {hit['url']}: {page.status_code}")
            continue
        pages.append(
            {
                "url": hit["url"],
                "title": hit["title"],
                "content": page.json()["results"][0]["markdown"],
            }
        )
    return pages


for page in research("eu ai act compliance deadlines"):
    print(f"--- {page['title']} ({page['url']})")
    print(page["content"][:500])
```

{% endcode %}
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

### AI agent integration

Connect the Web API directly to AI frameworks, coding assistants (Cursor, Claude Code), or custom agents.

#### Option 1: Integration Prompt

Paste the following complete prompt into an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to instruct it to build a custom integration following our technical specification:

{% code expandable="true" %}

```
Integrate the Oxylabs Web API into this project for live web search and page reading.

Read https://developers.oxylabs.io/products/web-api/for-agents.md and follow
it. It has the base URL, auth, both endpoint schemas, reference code, the error and retry
rules, and the checklist to satisfy. If the page does not load, stop and tell me; do not
reconstruct the API from memory.

Decide the path and tell me before writing anything:
- Will this project's own code call the API at runtime? -> write the client the page
  specifies, matching how this codebase already makes outbound HTTP calls.
- Is the web access for you during this session rather than for the project's code?
  -> install the MCP server and the skills, the way the page describes.

The key is in OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY or a .env here. If it is in neither, ask me. Never
print the key: not in code, logs, tests, or your replies to me.

Prove it works before writing tests: make one real search, scrape one URL from the
results, and show me both request ids. If a call returns 401, stop and tell me.

When a scrape comes back empty or skeletal, retry it once with run_js: true. If it is still
empty and the site is on a country TLD (.lt, .es, .co.uk), retry once more with run_js and
location set to that country, then report the page as unreadable.

Then add a test for the retry and error mapping against a mocked transport and run it.
If you cannot run commands in this environment, say so once and give me the exact
commands to run instead.

Report back: the path you took, each checklist item on the page marked done or not,
what I still need to do myself, and anything you could not finish. Do not ask me
whether to proceed; do the work.
```

{% endcode %}

The prompt points the agent at a single page with a full product source-of-truth: base URL, authorization, both endpoint schemas, reference code, error and retry rules, and an agent checklist.

You can find the complete agent specification reference in the [For Agents](/products/web-api/for-agents) page.

{% hint style="info" %}
**If the agent can't fetch URLs**, give it the full page instead. `for-agents.md` is plain Markdown and self-contained, so save it or paste it in above the prompt and drop the paragraph that names the URL. Keep the spec itself out of the prompt: the two retry rules are repeated there because an agent applies them mid-task, everything else belongs on the page so it can't drift.
{% endhint %}

#### Option 2: Agent skills

Install official agent skills to teach your AI agent research methodologies, source citation rules, and search-to-scrape execution:

```bash
npx skills add oxylabs/web-api-skills
```

For more installation options, see [Oxylabs Agent Skills](https://developers.oxylabs.io/ai-workflows/agent-skills).

#### Option 3: MCP server

Connect to or self-host our official MCP server to expose Web API search, scrape, and dedicated scraper tools directly to Claude Code, Cursor, or your custom AI agent by pointing your agent to the Oxylabs-hosted server – `https://mcp.oxylabs.io/web-api-mcp`:

<details>

<summary><i class="fa-claude">:claude:</i>  <strong>Claude Code</strong></summary>

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user oxylabs-web-api \
  https://mcp.oxylabs.io/web-api-mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ${OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY}"
```

</details>

<details>

<summary><i class="fa-openai">:openai:</i>  <strong>ChatGPT/Codex</strong></summary>

```bash
codex mcp add oxylabs-web-api \
  --url https://mcp.oxylabs.io/web-api-mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY
```

</details>

<details>

<summary><i class="fa-cursor">:cursor:</i>  <strong>Cursor</strong> (or other clients supporting custom headers)</summary>

For any client that supports remote MCP servers with custom headers, add the server URL and an `Authorization` header to the client's MCP configuration. For example, in Cursor's `mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oxylabs-web-api": {
      "url": "https://mcp.oxylabs.io/web-api-mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Field names can differ between clients – check your client's documentation for how to add a remote MCP server with headers.

</details>

To learn more about Web API MCP or how to self-host the official Oxylabs server server, see [MCP servers](https://developers.oxylabs.io/ai-workflows/mcp).

#### Skills or MCP?

<table data-header-hidden><thead><tr><th width="210"></th><th></th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td></td><td><a href="https://developers.oxylabs.io/ai-workflows/agent-skills"><strong>Skills</strong></a></td><td><a href="https://developers.oxylabs.io/ai-workflows/mcp"><strong>MCP server</strong></a></td></tr><tr><td>Gives the agent</td><td>Judgment: when to search, which sources to trust, how to cite</td><td>Typed tools it can call directly</td></tr><tr><td>Needs a running process</td><td>No</td><td>Yes</td></tr><tr><td>Works in</td><td>Agents that load skill directories</td><td>Any MCP client</td></tr></tbody></table>

Install the skills separately when you want them without a running server, or when you want migrate your codebase to Oxylabs.

# Authentication

Learn how to authenticate requests to Oxylabs Web API endpoints.

The Oxylabs Web API uses the **API key as Bearer Token** for authentication. Every HTTP request sent to the API must include your API key in the `Authorization` request header.

```http
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

{% hint style="warning" %}
**Bearer scheme is mandatory.** The API backend parses the `Authorization` header for a `Bearer` prefix. Standard HTTP Basic Authentication (`Authorization: Basic ...`) is not accepted on any `/v1/scrape` or `/v1/search` requests and will return a `401 Unauthorized` status code.
{% endhint %}

To verify your credentials, you can submit a minimal search query:

```bash
curl https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query": "oxylabs"}'
```

## Getting a key

1. Log in to the [Oxylabs dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io).
2. Create a **Web API** instance.
3. Generate an API key on that instance.
4. Export it where your application reads it (e.g. your OS terminal or the CLI terminal of the project workspace):

```bash
export OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
```

## Troubleshooting `401 Unauthorized` errors

An authentication failure returns an HTTP `401` status without a JSON response body. The status code itself indicates that the request was rejected.

<table><thead><tr><th width="219">Scenario</th><th>Cause</th><th>Solution</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>401</code> on new integration</td><td>Key missing, header misspelled, or trailing whitespace/newlines from copy-pasting.</td><td>Re-copy the key from the <a href="https://dashboard.oxylabs.io">dashboard</a>. Check for trailing newlines or shell quote mangling (<code>.strip()</code>).</td></tr><tr><td><code>401</code> with valid key format</td><td>Key belongs to a different Oxylabs product.</td><td>Confirm the key was generated specifically on a Web API instance in the dashboard.</td></tr><tr><td><code>401</code> on previously working key</td><td>Key has been revoked, replaced, or deleted.</td><td>Generate a new key on your active instance.</td></tr><tr><td><code>401</code> across all requests</td><td>The account subscription or instance is disabled.</td><td>Contact <a href="mailto:support@oxylabs.io">Oxylabs support</a> to re-enable the account.</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Recommended practices for manual integrations

{% hint style="warning" %}
An API key is a spending credential. Anyone holding it can consume your account quota.
{% endhint %}

<table data-header-hidden><thead><tr><th width="154"></th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Environment variables</strong></td><td>Store keys in environment variables (<code>OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY</code>) or dedicated secret managers (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, etc.). Avoid hardcoding keys in source code.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Key isolation</strong></td><td>Use separate Web API instances for development, staging, and production to isolate product credit consumption and allow independent credential rotation.</td></tr></tbody></table>


# /search

Learn how to use Oxylabs Web API /search endpoint to search the live web and collect ranked results.

The `/v1/search` endpoint performs live web searches and returns ranked organic results, including titles, snippets, URLs, position metadata, and related queries. It works as a discovery tool to identify authoritative web pages before passing target URLs to the [`/v1/scrape`](/products/web-api/scrape) endpoint for full-page extraction.

## Request sample

The endpoint accepts a JSON request body with the search **query**, **result limits**, and **geo-location** parameters.

```bash
curl https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "eu ai act compliance deadlines",
    "max_results": 3,
    "location": "DE"
  }'
```

### Request parameters

<table><thead><tr><th width="123">Parameter</th><th width="533">Description</th><th width="88">Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><mark style="background-color:green;"><code>query</code></mark></td><td>Search keyword or phrase (between <code>1</code> and <code>2,048</code> characters).</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>max_results</code></td><td>Number of organic search results to return (between <code>1</code> and <code>20</code>). Default: <code>10</code></td><td>integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>location</code></td><td>ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. <code>DE</code>, <code>US</code>) for localized search.</td><td>string</td></tr></tbody></table>

&#x20;    – mandatory parameter.

{% hint style="warning" %}
Unknown or misspelled parameters are rejected with an HTTP `400 Bad Request` status code, not ignored.
{% endhint %}

### Request optimization

<details>

<summary><strong><code>query</code></strong></summary>

It's recommended to write what a person would type into a search box. Keyword-shaped queries outperform sentence-shaped ones:

<table><thead><tr><th width="373">Instead of</th><th>Use</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>"Can you tell me what the compliance deadlines for the EU AI Act are?"</td><td><code>eu ai act compliance deadlines</code></td></tr><tr><td>"I want to know how much Figma costs per seat"</td><td><code>figma pricing per seat</code></td></tr></tbody></table>

One question per request. A compound query returns results that match neither half well.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong><code>max_results</code></strong></summary>

Parameter is a limit, not a target. A query with fewer matches returns fewer results, which are ordered best-first.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong><code>location</code></strong></summary>

Pricing, availability, language and rankings often shift by country.

ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code is the only accepted format (e.g. `DE`, `US`). A well-formed pair that isn't an assigned country is rejected with a `400` error code. Omitting the the parameter sets a `default` locale, which is optimal only when the answer is not location-sensitive.

</details>

## Output sample

```json
{
    "state": "done",
    "results": [
        {
            "title": "Implementation Timeline | EU Artificial Intelligence Act",
            "outline": [
                "Providers: Providers of GPAI models that have been placed on the market before this date need to be compliant with the AI Act by 2 August 2027. ... Member States: Deadline for Member States to report to the Commission on the status of the financial and human resources of the national competent ..."
            ],
            "url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
            "metadata": {
                "position": 1
            }
        },
        {
            "title": "EU AI Act Timeline: Key Compliance Dates & Deadlines Explained",
            "outline": [
                "While the EU Commission is working with member states to build out the reporting and monitoring infrastructure of the AI Act until August 2025, companies have several key areas to focus on: establishing a risk management system, implementing data governance measures, drawing up technical ..."
            ],
            "url": "https://www.dataguard.com/eu-ai-act/timeline",
            "metadata": {
                "position": 2
            }
        },
        {
            "title": "Timeline for the Implementation of the EU AI Act | AI Act Service Desk",
            "outline": [
                "The EU’s AI Act legislation applies progressively, with a full roll-out of the main application milestones foreseen by 2 August 2028."
            ],
            "url": "https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act",
            "metadata": {
                "position": 3
            }
        }
    ],
    "related_questions": [],
    "related_searches": [],
    "params": {
        "query": "eu ai act compliance deadlines",
        "location": "DE",
        "max_results": 3
    },
    "metadata": {
        "timestamp": 1791289627,
        "request_id": "1791289625962078444"
    }
}
```

{% hint style="warning" %}
**`outline`** is just a representative snippet. To get live data from the page itself, [scrape the URL](/products/web-api/scrape).
{% endhint %}

### Output dictionary

<table><thead><tr><th width="244">Field</th><th width="404.04296875">Description</th><th width="95.94140625">Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>state</code></td><td><code>"done"</code> on success. A search that encounters an upstream failure returns <code>500</code> with <code>state: "faulted"</code> (see <a href="/products/web-api/troubleshooting">Error codes</a>).</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>results</code></td><td>Ranked organic results, best first. Always present, so empty output means nothing matched.</td><td>array</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].title</code></td><td>Fetched page title.</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].outline[]</code></td><td>SERP result snippets. Truncated mid-sentence.</td><td>array of strings</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].url</code></td><td>Absolute URL of the result. Pass to <a href="/products/web-api/scrape"><code>/v1/scrape</code></a>.</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].metadata.position</code></td><td>Organic SERP position, starting at <code>1</code>.</td><td>integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>related_questions</code></td><td>"People also ask" question object containing <code>question</code>, <code>title</code>, and <code>snippet</code> (when available).</td><td>array</td></tr><tr><td><code>related_searches</code></td><td>Related search queries, each containing <code>query</code>.</td><td>array</td></tr><tr><td><code>params</code></td><td>Execution parameters including defaults.</td><td>object</td></tr><tr><td><code>metadata.timestamp</code></td><td>Unix timestamp in seconds.</td><td>integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>metadata.request_id</code></td><td>19-digit request handle. <strong>Include in support tickets.</strong></td><td>string</td></tr></tbody></table>

{% hint style="info" %}
`related_searches` is useful for query expansion when a first search comes back thin. It offers the phrasing that has more coverage behind it.
{% endhint %}


# /scrape

Learn how to use Oxylabs Web API /scrape endpoint to fetch and parse any web page in the format you want.

The `/v1/scrape` endpoint fetches web pages by URL, automatically handling headless rendering, proxy rotation, access challenges, and localization. It returns structured page data in Markdown, HTML, JSON, or as PNG screenshots.

## Request sample

The endpoint accepts a JSON payload defining the target URL, requested output formats, rendering options, and geo-location context.

```bash
curl https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/scrape \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
      "url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
      "output": ["markdown"]
  }'
```

### Request parameters

<table><thead><tr><th width="98">Parameter</th><th width="566">Description</th><th width="93">Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><mark style="background-color:green;"><code>url</code></mark></td><td>Absolute <code>http</code> / <code>https</code> target URL.</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>output</code></td><td>Response format: <code>markdown</code>, <code>html</code>, <code>json</code>, <code>screenshot</code>. Supports multiple values. Default: <code>html</code></td><td>array of strings</td></tr><tr><td><code>json</code></td><td>When <code>output: ["json"]</code>, can be used for custom AI parsing through <code>prompt</code> or <code>schema</code>. See <a href="/products/web-api/scrape/ai-parsing">AI Parsing</a>.</td><td>object</td></tr><tr><td><code>location</code></td><td>Two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., <code>"US"</code>, <code>"DE"</code>, <code>"JP"</code>).</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>device</code></td><td>User-agent and viewport emulation: <code>"desktop"</code> (default) or <code>"mobile"</code>. </td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>run_js</code></td><td>Enables JavaScript rendering when set to <code>true</code>. Default: <code>false</code>.</td><td>boolean</td></tr></tbody></table>

&#x20;    – mandatory parameter.

<details>

<summary><strong><code>output</code></strong></summary>

The `output` array allows fetching multiple output formats in a single request execution. Below is an example of combined output request:

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/product",
  "output": ["markdown", "json"],
  "json": {
    "prompt": "Extract the product name, stock status, and price as a number."
  }
}
```

<table data-header-hidden><thead><tr><th width="119"></th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>markdown</code></td><td>Converts the DOM tree into clean, structured Markdown, stripping navigation scripts and styling formatting. Optimized for ingestion into LLM context windows to minimize token usage.</td></tr><tr><td><code>html</code></td><td>The raw page markup. Use it when you need the markup itself (attributes, embedded JSON-LD, inline data). Not recommended for page content collection.</td></tr><tr><td><code>screenshot</code></td><td>Base64-encoded PNG image of the fully rendered page. <strong><code>run_js: true</code> is required</strong>, otherwise the request is rejected.</td></tr><tr><td><code>json</code></td><td>Structured extraction in the same request as the retrieval (no selectors to write or maintain). Describe the fields in a <code>prompt</code>, or pin their exact shape with a <code>schema</code>. See <a href="/products/web-api/scrape/ai-parsing">AI parsing</a>.</td></tr></tbody></table>

{% hint style="info" %}
**Exception:** `video` output format is available for `/scrape/media` [dedicated scrapers](/products/web-api/scrape/dedicated-scrapers).
{% endhint %}

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong><code>run_js</code></strong></summary>

Executes the page's own JavaScript before the content is captured.

Dropping `run_js` defaults to the optimal execution path for the given source path. Explicitly setting `"run_js": true` uses a headless browser instance to execute client-side scripts, dynamic XHR requests, and Single Page Application (SPA) rendering.

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/spa-dashboard",
  "output": ["markdown"],
  "run_js": true
}
```

* **Latency impact:** Headless browser rendering increases request duration significantly. Set client HTTP timeouts to at least `150` seconds. When high volume is required, [async delivery](/products/web-api/scrape/delivery-modes) is recommended.
* **Resource optimization:** Always try fetching content without it. For static pages or RSS/atom feeds, pass `"run_js": false` to maximize request throughput and minimize latency. Choose rendering only when necessary.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong><code>location</code></strong></summary>

Geo-targeting routes requests through localized proxy exit nodes. This ensures localized pricing, language variations, and region-exclusive content are served correctly.

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/pricing",
  "output": ["html"],
  "location": "DE",
  "check_empty_geo": true
}
```

{% hint style="info" %}
When using [Dedicated Scrapers](/products/web-api/scrape/dedicated-scrapers), some localization parameters may be named differently.
{% endhint %}

</details>

## Output sample

A successful request returns an HTTP `200 OK` status with a standard envelope. Fields inside `results[]` with unrequested output formats return `null`.

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "results": [
    {
      "html": null,
      "markdown": "# Implementation Timeline\n\nProviders need to be compliant...",
      "screenshot": null,
      "json": null,
      "metadata": {
        "page": 1,
        "run_js": false,
        "url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/"
      }
    }
  ],
  "params": {
    "url": "https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline/",
    "output": ["markdown"],
    "json": { "schema": null, "prompt": null },
    "location": null,
    "device": "desktop",
    "run_js": null
  },
  "metadata": {
    "timestamp": 1787431568,
    "request_id": "7503078851572948993"
  }
}
```

{% hint style="info" %}
**`results[]` field with unrequested output formats return `null`.** \
For example, asking for `["markdown"]` populates `markdown` and leaves `html`, `screenshot` and `json` as null. Any [dedicated scraper](/products/web-api/scrape/dedicated-scrapers) puts its structured fields under `json`.
{% endhint %}

### Output dictionary

<table><thead><tr><th width="208">Field</th><th>Description</th><th width="92">Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>status</code></td><td>HTTP status code, <code>200</code> on success. See <a href="/products/web-api/troubleshooting">Error codes</a>.</td><td>integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>results</code></td><td>One entry for the requested URL.</td><td>array</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].markdown</code></td><td>Page as Markdown, if requested. <code>null</code> otherwise.</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].html</code></td><td>Raw result markup, if requested. <code>null</code> otherwise.</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].json</code></td><td>Parsed fields from a <a href="/products/web-api/scrape/dedicated-scrapers">dedicated scraper</a> or <a href="/products/web-api/scrape/ai-parsing">AI parser</a>, if requested <code>null</code> otherwise.</td><td>object</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].screenshot</code></td><td>Base64-encoded image string, if requested. <code>null</code> otherwise.</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>results[].metadata.url</code></td><td>Fetched URL for scraping after redirects.</td><td>string</td></tr><tr><td><code>params</code></td><td>All parameters use for the requests with applied defaults.</td><td>object</td></tr><tr><td><code>metadata.timestamp</code></td><td>Unix timestamp in seconds.</td><td>integer</td></tr><tr><td><code>metadata.request_id</code></td><td>Identifier for this request. <strong>Include it in support tickets.</strong></td><td>string</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Latency and concurrency

A scrape renders a real page with budget in **seconds, not milliseconds**. We recommend a couple of of safe practices to build around that:

<table data-header-hidden><thead><tr><th width="123"></th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Client timeout</strong></td><td>150 seconds is a safe default, while a 10-second timeout may fail on pages that would have succeeded. For higher volume (e.g. media, large SERP runs, etc.) with a risk of client timeout, run the same scrapers with async delivery instead of blocking the request. See <a href="/products/web-api/scrape/delivery-modes">Delivery Modes</a>.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Concurrency limit</strong></td><td>Scraping ten search results in parallel multiplies cost and latency for pages you won't read. Scrape the two or three that plausibly answer the question and only increase concurrency gradually until <code>429</code> error is reached.</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Dedicated scrapers

Beyond generic URL scraping, target-specific scrapers can be used with `POST /v1/scrape/{target}/{collection}`. They accept target-specific parameters (e.g., ASINs, browse nodes, store zip codes) and return structured fields under `results[].json`:

```bash
curl https://webapi.oxylabs.io/v1/scrape/amazon/product \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "B0935DN1BN",
    "output": ["json"],
    "location": "10115",
    "domain": "de",
    "currency": "EUR"
  }'
```

See [Dedicated scrapers](/products/web-api/scrape/dedicated-scrapers) for target overviews (Google, Amazon, YouTube, Bing, AI & LLMs, Commerce, etc.).


# Dedicated Scrapers

Discover Oxylabs Web API dedicated scrapers for structured field extraction from specialized web targets.

Beyond the generic [`/scrape`](/products/web-api/scrape) scraper, Web API offers purpose-built and actively maintained scrapers for specific targets:

```http
POST /v1/scrape/{target}/{collection}
```

The **generic scraper hands you the whole page**, while a **dedicated scraper hands you the fields** on that page, such as product price and availability, a SERP's organic positions and ads, a video's duration and view count, etc. Results are parsed and named, with the parser maintained by Oxylabs when the site's markup changes.

{% hint style="success" %}
This page covers the basics across targets and their specialized endpoints. To get an up-to-date dedicated scrapers list and and their parameters, use [Endpoint Discovery](/products/web-api/scrape/endpoint-discovery). A reference endpoint and parameter tables are found in the [**API Reference**](/api-reference).
{% endhint %}

## Which endpoint to call

Each endpoint takes either a `query` or a `url` (not both):

<table data-header-hidden><thead><tr><th width="129"></th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong><code>query</code></strong><br><em>(recommended)</em></td><td><p><strong>If you have an identifier or a search term.</strong></p><pre class="language-json"><code class="lang-json">POST /v1/scrape/amazon/product
{ "query": "B07FZ8S74R", "output": ["json"] }
</code></pre><p>Identifier or search term (e.g., ASIN on <code>/amazon/product</code>, a keyword on <code>/amazon/search</code>, a video ID on <code>/youtube/metadata</code>, etc.). The endpoint builds the URL for you.</p></td></tr><tr><td><strong><code>url</code></strong></td><td><p><strong>If you already have the URL.</strong></p><pre class="language-json"><code class="lang-json">POST /v1/scrape/amazon
{ "url": "https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07FZ8S74R", "output": ["json"] }
</code></pre><p>URL you already have from a <a href="/products/web-api/search"><code>/search</code></a> result or your own data. The target-level endpoint (<code>/amazon</code>, <code>/walmart</code>, no <code>{collection}</code> segment) takes a URL on that site and picks the correct parser from its shape.</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

## Target overview

<table><thead><tr><th width="170">Target</th><th width="236">Endpoints</th><th>Capabilities</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="/api-reference/dedicated-scrapers/search-engine-scrapers">Google</a></td><td><code>/google/search</code>,<br><code>/google/ads</code>,<br><code>/google/aimode</code>,<br><code>/google/shopping</code>,<br><code>/google/maps</code>,<br><code>/google/lens</code>,<br><code>/google/trends</code></td><td>Organic SERPs, Google Ads, AI Overviews, AI Mode answers, local business listings, product search.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="/api-reference/dedicated-scrapers/commerce-scrapers">Amazon</a></td><td><code>/amazon/product</code>,<br><code>/amazon/search</code>,<br><code>/amazon/pricing</code>,<br><code>/amazon/sellers</code>,<br><code>/amazon/bestsellers</code></td><td>Product details, search results, Buy Box offer listings across all sellers, category bestsellers.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="/api-reference/dedicated-scrapers/media-scrapers">YouTube</a></td><td><code>/media/youtube/metadata</code>,<br><code>/media/youtube/subtitles</code>,<br><code>/media/youtube/download</code>,<br><code>/media/youtube/search</code></td><td>Video metadata, clean subtitles, media clip downloads, AI trainability permission flags.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="/api-reference/dedicated-scrapers/media-scrapers">Media</a></td><td><code>/media</code></td><td>Media file download from various sources (TikTok, BiliBili, and more).</td></tr><tr><td><a href="/api-reference/dedicated-scrapers/search-engine-scrapers">Bing</a></td><td><code>/bing/search</code>,<br><code>/bing</code></td><td>Organic Bing SERPs for multi-engine comparisons.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="/api-reference/dedicated-scrapers/llm-and-ai-scrapers">AI &#x26; LLMs</a></td><td><code>/chatgpt</code>,<br><code>/gemini</code>,<br><code>/perplexity</code></td><td>Query conversational AI assistants and extract generated text and cited sources (Async only).</td></tr><tr><td><a href="/api-reference/dedicated-scrapers/commerce-scrapers">Commerce &#x26; Retail</a></td><td><code>/walmart</code>,<br><code>/target</code>,<br><code>/ebay</code>,<br><code>/etsy</code>,<br><code>/aliexpress</code>,<br><code>/kroger</code>,<br><code>/homeimprovement</code>,<br>&#x26; more...</td><td>Product specifications, local inventory, fulfillment pricing, seller storefronts, etc.</td></tr></tbody></table>

{% hint style="info" %}
For full reference of parameter indexes, technical specs, and schemas per endpoint, see the [API Reference](/api-reference). For an up-to-date list of dedicated scraper and parameters use [Endpoint Discovery](/products/web-api/scrape/endpoint-discovery).
{% endhint %}

### Quick scraper reference

<details>

<summary><strong>Full scraper list</strong></summary>

{% hint style="warning" %}
This list is generated from `GET /v1/scrapers` plus `OPTIONS` on each endpoint. For up-to-date list of all available dedicated scrapers and their parameters, we recommend using the discovery endpoint. See [Endpoint Discovery](/products/web-api/scrape/endpoint-discovery).
{% endhint %}

Most dedicated scrapers exist in two variants:

* `/v1/scrape/...` returns the result in the response (sync/realtime)
* `/v1/async/scrape/...` returns a job and accepts `callback_url` (async)

A few of the dedicated scrapers run only as jobs, some also support batch of values. Learn more in [Delivery Modes](/products/web-api/scrape/delivery-modes).

<table><thead><tr><th>Endpoint</th><th width="169">Modes</th><th>Target-specific parameters</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape</code></td><td>sync · async · batch</td><td><code>url</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/alibaba</code></td><td>sync · async</td><td><code>url</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/alibaba/product</code></td><td>sync · async</td><td><code>query</code>, <code>domain</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/alibaba/search</code></td><td>sync · async</td><td><code>query</code>, <code>domain</code>, <code>start_page</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/aliexpress</code></td><td>sync · async</td><td><code>url</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/aliexpress/product</code></td><td>sync · async</td><td><code>query</code>, <code>domain</code>, <code>subdomain</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/aliexpress/search</code></td><td>sync · async</td><td><code>query</code>, <code>domain</code>, <code>start_page</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/allegro/product</code></td><td>sync · async</td><td><code>query</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/allegro/search</code></td><td>sync · async</td><td><code>query</code>, <code>delivery_time</code>, <code>domain</code>, <code>shipping_from</code>, <code>start_page</code>, <code>store_city</code>, <code>store_region</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>/v1/scrape/amazon</code></td><td>sync · async ·
