***

## City

Target proxies in specific cities by combining the `city` parameter with a matching country code (`cc`). Multi-word city names use underscores instead of spaces (e.g., `new_york`, `rio_de_janeiro`).

```
customer-USERNAME-cc-US-city-los_angeles:PASSWORD
```

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-city-munich:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import urllib.request
import random
username = 'USERNAME'
password = 'PASSWORD'
country = 'DE'
city = 'munich'
entry = ('http://customer-%s-cc-%s-city-%s:%s@pr.oxylabs.io:7777' %
    (username, country, city, password))
query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({
    'http': entry,
    'https': entry,
})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$country = 'DE';
$city = 'munich';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-cc-$country-city-$city:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Java" %}

```java
package example;

import org.apache.http.HttpHost;
import org.apache.http.client.fluent.*;

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        HttpHost entry = new HttpHost("pr.oxylabs.io", 7777);
        String query = Executor.newInstance()
            .auth(entry, "customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-city-munich", "PASS")
            .execute(Request.Get("http://ip.oxylabs.io/location").viaProxy(entry))
            .returnContent().asString();
        System.out.println(query);
    }
}
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="C#" %}

```csharp
using System;
using System.Net;

class Example
{
    static void Main()
    {
        var client = new WebClient();
        client.Proxy = new WebProxy("pr.oxylabs.io:7777");
        client.Proxy.Credentials = new NetworkCredential("customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-city-munich", "PASSWORD");
        Console.WriteLine(client.DownloadString("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location"));
    }
}
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Ruby" %}

```ruby
require 'uri'
require 'net/http'

uri = URI.parse('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location')
proxy = Net::HTTP::Proxy('pr.oxylabs.io', 7777, 'customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-city-munich', 'PASSWORD')

req = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri.path)

result = proxy.start(uri.host,uri.port) do |http|
    http.request(req)
end

puts result.body
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

Download the list of supported cities by clicking the file below:

{% file src="/files/628qdEipraPVtaUrEWuA" %}

{% hint style="info" %}
We support every city in the world, yet due to the dynamic nature of Residential Proxies we do not guarantee we will have proxies there at specific moment in time. Most popular cities are well covered.
{% endhint %}

## State

Select proxies from specific US states using the `st` parameter. State names must include the `us_` prefix (e.g., `us_california`, `us_illinois`).

```
customer-USERNAME-st-us_california:PASSWORD
```

#### Code Examples

In this example, a query to `ip.oxylabs.io/location` is performed from a random IP address from California, USA:

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-st-us_california:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

```php

$password = 'PASSWORD';
$state = 'us_california';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';

curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-st-$state:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

## Continent

Route requests through any of the seven continents using the `cn` parameter followed by a two-letter continent code:

`cn-AF` – Africa\
`cn-AN` – Antarctica\
`cn-AS` – Asia\
`cn-EU` – Europe\
`cn-NA` – North America\
`cn-OC` – Oceania\
`cn-SA` – South America

```
customer-USERNAME-cn-EU:PASSWORD
```

#### Code example

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-cn-AS:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$continent = 'AS';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-cn-$continent:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

## ZIP / Postal code

Target specific US 5-digit ZIP codes using the `postalcode` parameter. The parameter must be used with the country code parameter `cc` and a case-insensitive country code in 2-letter [**3166-1 alpha-2 format**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2).

{% hint style="info" %}
Currently we support **only US-based codes** for ZIP code targeting, the parameter **must be accompanied by** `cc-US`.
{% endhint %}

```
customer-USERNAME-cc-US-postalcode-90210:PASSWORD
```

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-cc-US-postalcode-90210:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$country = 'US';
$postalcode = '90210';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-cc-$country-postalcode-$postalcode:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import urllib.request
import random

password = 'PASSWORD'

postalcode = '90210'

    (username, country, postalcode, password))

    'http': entry,
    'https': entry,
})

print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())
```

## Geohash

Target proxies within specific geographic grid cells using geohash codes ranging from Level 1 (largest) to Level 4 (smallest). Geohash allows precise grid-based targeting without relying on traditional administrative boundaries like country or city borders.

By default, geohash uses strict targeting: if no IP is available in the requested cell, the request returns a `502 Bad Gateway` error.

```
customer-USERNAME-geohash-u09:PASSWORD
```

<table><thead><tr><th width="79">Length</th><th width="205.69921875">Approx. cell size</th><th>Examples</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>1</td><td>≤ 5,000 km × 5,000 km</td><td><code>geohash-9</code> (Large part of US &#x26; Mexico), <code>geohash-c</code> (Northern US &#x26; Canada)</td></tr><tr><td>2</td><td>≤ 1,250 km × 625 km</td><td><code>geohash-gc</code> (Ireland, Northern Ireland, England and Scotland)</td></tr><tr><td>3</td><td>≤ 156 km × 156 km</td><td><code>geohash-u09</code> (Paris)</td></tr><tr><td>4</td><td>≤ 39.1 km × 19.5 km</td><td><code>geohash-drq4</code> (Most of Nantucket Island)</td></tr></tbody></table>

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-geohash-u09:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$geohash = 'u09';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-geohash-$geohash:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import urllib.request
import random
username = 'USERNAME'
password = 'PASSWORD'
geohash = 'u09'
entry = ('http://customer-%s-geohash-%s:%s@pr.oxylabs.io:7777' %
    (username, geohash, password))
query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({
    'http': entry,
    'https': entry,
})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Java" %}

```java

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        HttpHost entry = new HttpHost("pr.oxylabs.io", 7777);
        String query = Executor.newInstance()
            .auth(entry, "customer-USERNAME-geohash-u09", "PASS")
            .execute(Request.Get("http://ip.oxylabs.io/location").viaProxy(entry))
            .returnContent().asString();
        System.out.println(query);
    }
}
```

{% endtab %}

```csharp
    static void Main()
    {

    }
```

```ruby
    http.request(req)
end

puts result.body
```

### Geohash fallback

{% hint style="warning" %}
`geohash` and `geohash_fallback` are mutually exclusive with each other and with other geo-location parameters, such as `cc` (country), `city`, `st` (state), `cn` (continent), and `postalcode`.
{% endhint %}

If your use case does not require a strict cell match, `geohash_fallback` uses the rotator that automatically removes one geohash character at a time to expand the area until an available proxy is found.&#x20;

If no IP is found at single-character level, a `502 Bad Gateway` error is returned.

```
customer-USERNAME-geohash_fallback-2svd:PASSWORD
```

* **Initial target:** `2svd` (≤ 39.1 km × 19.5 km)
* **Fallback 1 (1 character removed):** `2sv` (≤ 156 km × 156 km)
* **Fallback 2 (2 characters removed):** `2s` (≤ 1,250 km × 625 km)
* **Fallback 3 (3 characters removed):** `2` (≤ 5,000 km × 5,000 km)

{% hint style="info" %}
**Tracking the fallback:** geohash cell that was used is returned in the `x-geo-hash-fallback` response header. Compare it with your requested value to see if a fallback occurred and how far the area was expanded.
{% endhint %}

#### Code example

```shellscript
curl -v -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-geohash_fallback-2svd:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

***

## ASN targeting

Route traffic through specific Internet Service Provider (ISP) networks using Autonomous System Numbers (`ASN`). You can find ASN numbers [**here**](https://asnlookup.com/)**.**

```
customer-USERNAME-ASN-21928-sessid-abcde12345:PASSWORD
```

If no active proxies are available for the specified ASN, the request returns a `502 Bad Gateway` error.

{% hint style="warning" %}
Accessing Residential Proxies from certain ASNs can return a `403 Access denied: restricted ASN` error if KYC verification is not completed for your Oxylabs account. [Contact support](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) to complete KYC process.
{% endhint %}

{% hint style="info" %}
You can use either Country or ASN parameter per each request. If both location parameters are used, only Country parameter will be applied.
{% endhint %}

***

## Coordinates

Target proxies near specific geographic coordinates using the `X-Oxylabs-Geolocation` HTTP proxy header. Value format is `Latitude:Longitude;Radius` (radius in miles, minimum 10 miles).

```
X-Oxylabs-Geolocation: 49.9235:-97.0811;10
```

{% hint style="info" %}
If no IP is found within the provided coordinates and radius, you will receive `502` response code. See full list of response codes [**here**](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/additional-information).
{% endhint %}

#### Code example

```bash
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD" --proxy-header "X-Oxylabs-Geolocation: 49.9235:-97.0811;10" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

## China entry nodes

For requests initiated from mainland China, dedicated HTTPS regional entry nodes provide optimized connectivity.

* **Hong Kong:** `a81298871.com:8000`
* **Beijing:** `cnt9t1is.com:8000`

```bash
curl -x cnt9t1is.com:8000 -U "customer-USERNAME-cc-US:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% hint style="warning" %}
**Note:** Some third-party tools may not work with Hong Kong and Beijing entry nodes. Confirmed working tools include [Oxy Proxy Extension for Chrome](https://developers.oxylabs.io/integrations/proxy-integrations/oxy-proxy-extension-for-chrome), [SwitchyOmega](https://developers.oxylabs.io/integrations/proxy-integrations/switchyomega), and [Shadowrocket](https://developers.oxylabs.io/integrations/proxy-integrations/shadowrocket). We are currently working on supporting more integrations for HTTPS protocol.

If you are connecting to our residential network from China and still have issues with provided entry nodes, please get in touch at [**support@oxylabs.io**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) for additional help.
{% endhint %}


# Session Control & IP Rotation

Learn how to manage Residential Proxy sessions to keep the same IP address across multiple requests and control session length and IP rotation.

Oxylabs Residential Proxies rotate automatically with every request by default. To keep the same IP address for sequential requests, configure sticky session parameters in your username string or connect via sticky proxy entry ports.

<table><thead><tr><th width="156">Method</th><th width="132">Parameter</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="#default-sticky-sessions-sessid"><strong>Sticky session</strong></a></td><td><code>sessid</code></td><td>Automatically rotates to a new IP to keep the session active. 10 minutes (default).</td></tr><tr><td><a href="#extend-session-duration-sesstime"><strong>Session duration</strong></a></td><td><code>sesstime</code></td><td>Extends <code>sessid</code> lifetime. Session ends once the timer expires. Up to 1440 min (24 hrs)</td></tr><tr><td><a href="#single-ip-strict-session-binding-sessid_oneip"><strong>Single-IP binding</strong></a></td><td><code>sessid_oneip</code></td><td>Binds strictly to a single exit node. Fails with HTTP <code>502</code> if IP drops. Up to 1440 min (24 hrs)</td></tr><tr><td><a href="#sticky-proxy-entry-nodes-port-range"><strong>Sticky ports</strong></a></td><td>Port range</td><td>Port-based stickiness (ports <code>10001–49999</code>) requires no username-based parameters. Up to 10 minutes.</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Default sticky sessions (`sessid`)

The `sessid` parameter routes multiple requests through the same IP address as long as the IP is online. Add `sessid` after your `username` with a random alphanumeric string (e.g. `sessid-abcd1234`):

```
customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-sessid-abcd1234:PASSWORD
```

By default, a session lasts 10 minutes, or ends after 60 seconds without any requests – whichever comes first. Once that happens, a new IP address is assigned automatically so your requests continue uninterrupted. To change the session length, please refer to [Extend session duration](#extend-session-duration-sesstime).

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-sessid-abcd1234:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$country = 'DE';
$session = mt_rand();
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-cc-$country-sessid-$session:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import urllib.request
import random
username = 'USERNAME'
password = 'PASSWORD'
country = 'DE'
session = random.random()
entry = ('http://customer-%s-cc-%s-sessid-%s:%s@pr.oxylabs.io:7777' %
    (username, country, session, password))
query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({
    'http': entry,
    'https': entry,
})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Java" %}

```java
package example;

import java.io.*;
import java.util.Random;
import org.apache.http.HttpHost;
import org.apache.http.auth.*;
import org.apache.http.client.CredentialsProvider;
import org.apache.http.client.fluent.Request;
import org.apache.http.client.methods.*;
import org.apache.http.impl.client.*;
import org.apache.http.impl.conn.BasicHttpClientConnectionManager;
import org.apache.http.util.EntityUtils;

class Client {
    public static final String username = "USERNAME";
    public static final String password = "PASSWORD";
    public String session_id = Integer.toString(new Random().nextInt(Integer.MAX_VALUE));
    public CloseableHttpClient client;

    public Client(String country) {
        String login = "customer-"+username+(country!=null ? "-cc-"+country : "")
            +"-sessid-" + session_id;
        HttpHost entry_node = new HttpHost("pr.oxylabs.io:7777");
        CredentialsProvider credentials_provider = new BasicCredentialsProvider();
        credentials_provider.setCredentials(new AuthScope(entry_node),
            new UsernamePasswordCredentials(login, password));
        client = HttpClients.custom()
            .setConnectionManager(new BasicHttpClientConnectionManager())
            .setProxy(entry_node)
            .setDefaultCredentialsProvider(credentials_provider)
            .build();
    }

    public String request(String url) throws IOException {
        HttpGet request = new HttpGet(url);
        CloseableHttpResponse response = client.execute(request);
        try {
            return EntityUtils.toString(response.getEntity());
        } finally { response.close(); }
    }

    public void close() throws IOException { client.close(); }
}

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Client client = new Client("de");
        try {
            System.out.println(client.request("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location"));
        } finally { client.close(); }
    }
}
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="C#" %}

```csharp
using System;
using System.Net;

class Client : WebClient
{
    public static string username = "USERNAME";
    public static string password = "PASSWORD";
    public string session_id = new Random().Next().ToString();

    public Client(string country_iso = null)
    {
        this.Proxy = new WebProxy("pr.oxylabs.io:7777");
        var login = "customer-"+username+(country_iso != null ? "-cc-"+country_iso : "")
            +"-sessid-"+session_id;
        this.Proxy.Credentials = new NetworkCredential(login, password);
    }

    protected override WebRequest GetWebRequest(Uri address)
    {
        var request = base.GetWebRequest(address) as HttpWebRequest;
        request.ConnectionGroupName = session_id;
        return request;
    }
}

class Example
{
    static void Main()
    {
        var client = new Client("de");
        Console.WriteLine(client.DownloadString("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location"));
    }
}
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Ruby" %}

```ruby
require 'uri'
require 'net/http'
require 'net/https'

entry_node = 'pr.oxylabs.io'
entry_port = '7777'
username = 'USERNAME'
password = 'PASSWORD'
session_id = Random.rand(1000000)

uri = URI.parse("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location")
headers = {
    'Accept-Encoding' => 'gzip'
}

proxy = Net::HTTP::Proxy(entry_node, entry_port, "#{username}-cc-DE-sessid-#{session_id}", password)
http = proxy.new(uri.host,uri.port)

if uri.scheme == 'https'
    http.use_ssl = true
    http.verify_mode = OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_NONE
end

req = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri.path, headers)

result = http.start do |con|
    con.request(req)
end

puts result.body
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

## Extend session duration (`sesstime`)

Combine the `sesstime` parameter with `sessid` to extend session duration beyond the 10-minute default (or up to 60 seconds of inactivity) up to 1440 minutes (24 hours). Specify duration in minutes (e.g., `sesstime-30` for 30 minutes):

```
customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-sessid-abcd1234-sesstime-30:PASSWORD
```

{% hint style="info" %}
**Note:** Session time parameter does not guarantee that all of your requests finish before the session ends. The session expires once the time limit is reached, even if some requests are still in progress.
{% endhint %}

{% hint style="warning" %}
Because residential proxy IP availability is dynamic, an individual exit node may disconnect before your specified session time expires. If an exit node drops, `sessid` will automatically rotate to a new IP to fulfill your request.&#x20;
{% endhint %}

#### Code examples

We chose the same German IP as in the previous example, this time we are adding `sessid` string and `sesstime` parameter for 7 minutes:

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-sessid-abcd1234-sesstime-7:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$country = 'DE';
$session = mt_rand();
$sesstime = 7;
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-cc-$country-sessid-$session-sesstime-$sesstime:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

```python

password = 'PASSWORD'
country = 'DE'
session = random.random()
sesstime = 7
entry = ('http://customer-%s-cc-%s-sessid-%s-sesstime-%d:%s@pr.oxylabs.io:7777' %
    (username, country, city, session, sesstime, password))
query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({
    'http': entry,
    'https': entry,
})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())
```

```java
package example;

import java.io.*;
import java.util.Random;
import org.apache.http.HttpHost;
import org.apache.http.auth.*;
import org.apache.http.client.CredentialsProvider;
import org.apache.http.client.fluent.Request;
import org.apache.http.client.methods.*;
import org.apache.http.impl.client.*;
import org.apache.http.impl.conn.BasicHttpClientConnectionManager;
import org.apache.http.util.EntityUtils;

class Client {
    public static final String username = "USERNAME";
    public static final String password = "PASSWORD";
    public String session_id = Integer.toString(new Random().nextInt(Integer.MAX_VALUE));
    public String sesstime = "7";
    public CloseableHttpClient client;

    public Client(String country) {
        String login = "customer-"+username+(country_iso != null ? "-cc-"+country_iso : "")+"-sessid-"+session_id+"-sesstime-" +sesstime;
        HttpHost entry_node = new HttpHost("pr.oxylabs.io:7777");
        CredentialsProvider credentials_provider = new BasicCredentialsProvider();
        credentials_provider.setCredentials(new AuthScope(entry_node),
            new UsernamePasswordCredentials(login, password));
        client = HttpClients.custom()
            .setConnectionManager(new BasicHttpClientConnectionManager())
            .setProxy(entry_node)
            .setDefaultCredentialsProvider(credentials_provider)
            .build();
    }

    public String request(String url) throws IOException {
        HttpGet request = new HttpGet(url);
        CloseableHttpResponse response = client.execute(request);
        try {
            return EntityUtils.toString(response.getEntity());
        } finally { response.close(); }
    }

    public void close() throws IOException { client.close(); }
}

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Client client = new Client("de");
        try {
            System.out.println(client.request("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location"));
        } finally { client.close(); }
    }
}
```

## Single-IP session binding (`sessid_oneip`)

Use `sessid_oneip` instead of `sessid` when your workflow requires strict IP consistency and cannot tolerate IP rotation mid-session.&#x20;

Unlike standard sticky sessions, if the assigned exit node goes offline, the system will not rotate to a new IP, and instead the request fails with an HTTP `502 Bad Gateway` error. When a `502` occurs, initiate a new session using a fresh `sessid_oneip` string. `sessid_oneip` can be combined with `sesstime` in the same way as `sessid`.

```
customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-sessid_oneip-qwert-sesstime-10:PASSWORD
```

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-cc-DE-sessid_oneip-abcd1234:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$country = 'DE';
$session = mt_rand();
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-cc-$country-sessid_oneip-$session:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python

password = 'PASSWORD'

    'http': entry,
    'https': entry,
})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())
```

```java
package example;

import java.io.*;
import java.util.Random;
import org.apache.http.HttpHost;
import org.apache.http.auth.*;
import org.apache.http.client.CredentialsProvider;
import org.apache.http.client.fluent.Request;
import org.apache.http.client.methods.*;
import org.apache.http.impl.client.*;
import org.apache.http.impl.conn.BasicHttpClientConnectionManager;
import org.apache.http.util.EntityUtils;

class Client {
    public static final String username = "USERNAME";
    public static final String password = "PASSWORD";
    public String session_id = Integer.toString(new Random().nextInt(Integer.MAX_VALUE));
    public CloseableHttpClient client;

    public Client(String country) {
        String login = "customer-"+username+(country!=null ? "-cc-"+country : "")
            +"-sessid_oneip-" + session_id;
        HttpHost entry_node = new HttpHost("pr.oxylabs.io:7777");
        CredentialsProvider credentials_provider = new BasicCredentialsProvider();
        credentials_provider.setCredentials(new AuthScope(entry_node),
            new UsernamePasswordCredentials(login, password));
        client = HttpClients.custom()
            .setConnectionManager(new BasicHttpClientConnectionManager())
            .setProxy(entry_node)
            .setDefaultCredentialsProvider(credentials_provider)
            .build();
    }

    public String request(String url) throws IOException {
        HttpGet request = new HttpGet(url);
        CloseableHttpResponse response = client.execute(request);
        try {
            return EntityUtils.toString(response.getEntity());
        } finally { response.close(); }
    }

    public void close() throws IOException { client.close(); }
}

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Client client = new Client("de");
        try {
            System.out.println(client.request("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location"));
        } finally { client.close(); }
    }
}
```

## Sticky proxy entry nodes (Port range)

Connect to country-specific entry node points on dedicated port ranges (`10001–49999`) to maintain an IP address for up to 10 minutes without passing `sessid` parameters in your username string. Reusing the same port keeps the same exit node, while changing the port assigns a new sticky IP.

{% hint style="info" %}
Country-specific sticky entry ports support standard username/password and IP Whitelisting authentication, but do not support city or state-level parameters.&#x20;
{% endhint %}

See the [**Oxylabs dashboard**](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/en/) for entry point information, download a complete list of sticky entry points, or see them in the table below.

{% file src="/files/9iaqY6oaoc8X7lW6q31e" %}

<details>

<summary><strong>Full list of sticky proxy entry nodes</strong></summary>

{% hint style="success" %}
Feel free to use the table search bar below for easier navigation.
{% endhint %}

| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <p>Great Britain<br>gb-pr.oxylabs.io:20001 - 29999</p>            | <p>Germany<br>de-pr.oxylabs.io:30001 - 39999</p>                | <p>France<br>fr-pr.oxylabs.io:40001 - 49999</p>                 |

```python
import urllib.request

username = 'USERNAME'
password = 'PASSWORD'
entry = ('http://customer-%s:%s@tr-pr.oxylabs.io:30001' %
    (username, password))
query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({
    'http': entry,
    'https': entry,
})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())
```

```java
package example;

import org.apache.http.HttpHost;
import org.apache.http.client.fluent.*;

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        HttpHost entry = new HttpHost("tr-pr.oxylabs.io", 30001);
        String query = Executor.newInstance()
            .auth(entry, "customer-USERNAME", "PASS")
            .execute(Request.Get("http://ip.oxylabs.io/location").viaProxy(entry))
            .returnContent().asString();
        System.out.println(query);
    }
}
```

# Protocols

Explore supported Residential Proxy protocols and learn how to configure HTTP, HTTPS, HTTPS/3, and SOCKS5 connections.

Oxylabs Residential Proxies support `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, `HTTP/3`, and `SOCKS5` connection protocols. You can choose the protocol that best fits your scraping stack, HTTP library, or third-party software.

<table><thead><tr><th width="93">Protocol</th><th width="247">Gateway</th><th width="114">Transport</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="#http-protocol"><strong>HTTP</strong></a></td><td><code>pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td><td>TCP</td><td>Default connection method supported by all libraries and tools.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="#https-protocol"><strong>HTTPS</strong></a></td><td><code>https://pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td><td>TCP / SSL</td><td>Fully encrypted connection to the proxy gateway.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="#http-3-protocol"><strong>HTTP/3</strong></a></td><td><code>socks.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td><td>UDP / QUIC</td><td>Requires a SOCKS5 proxy with UDP support.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="#socks5-protocol"><strong>SOCKS5</strong></a></td><td><code>socks5h://pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td><td>TCP / UDP</td><td>Low-level proxying. Requires username flags for geo-targeting.</td></tr></tbody></table>

## HTTP

The standard `HTTP` protocol is the primary connection method for Oxylabs Residential Proxies that's supported out of the box by all HTTP client libraries, web scraping frameworks, and third-party tools.

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```bash
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

```python
import requests

    'http': 'http://customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD@pr.oxylabs.io:7777',
    'https': 'http://customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD@pr.oxylabs.io:7777',
}

response = requests.get('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location', proxies=proxies)
print(response.text)
```

{% endtab %}

## HTTPS

Connecting via `HTTPS` provides an end-to-end encrypted SSL connection to the proxy entry node. To enable HTTPS proxying, add `https://` to your proxy entry point (e.g., `https://pr.oxylabs.io:7777`). Same applies when using `HTTPS` with [country-specific entry nodes](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#country-specific-entry-nodes).

{% hint style="info" %}
Verify that your specific `HTTP` client library or 3-rd party tool supports `HTTPS` protocol before use, as legacy tools may default to unencrypted `HTTP` proxy connections.
{% endhint %}

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```bash
curl -x https://pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import requests

proxies = {
    'http': 'https://customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD@pr.oxylabs.io:7777',
    'https': 'https://customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD@pr.oxylabs.io:7777',
}

response = requests.get('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location', proxies=proxies)
print(response.text)
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Node.js (axios)" %}

```javascript
const axios = require('axios');

axios.get('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location', {
  proxy: {
    protocol: 'https',
    host: 'pr.oxylabs.io',
    port: 7777,
    auth: {
      username: 'customer-USERNAME',
      password: 'PASSWORD'
    }
  }
})
.then(response => console.log(response.data))
.catch(error => console.error(error));
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

## **HTTP/3 (MASQUE)**

{% hint style="warning" %}
**Note:** `Google` is a restricted target to use with `UDP` connection.
{% endhint %}

Oxylabs Residential Proxies support native `UDP` and `HTTP/3` tunneling via MASQUE ([RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9298.html)).

Traditional proxies force traffic through `TCP` connections (via `HTTP CONNECT` or `SOCKS5`), causing `HTTP/3` requests to downgrade to `HTTP/1.1` or `HTTP/2`. MASQUE maintains an end-to-end `QUIC` connection through our residential exit nodes, allowing your client to transmit native `UDP` traffic directly to modern target destinations.

The MASQUE service runs over `QUIC` on a dedicated `UDP` port:

```
masque.oxylabs.io:50000
```

{% hint style="info" %}
**Note:** Ensure your firewall allows outbound `UDP` traffic on port `50000`.
{% endhint %}

### Use cases <a href="#use-cases" id="use-cases"></a>

* **Native HTTP/3 Web Scraping:** Scrape modern target websites without triggering protocol downgrade flags.
* **DNS Resolution over UDP:** Execute direct DNS queries (`53/udp`) via residential IPs.
* **Real-Time UDP Protocols:** Route WebRTC, SIP, or gaming traffic requiring true UDP connection.

{% hint style="info" %}
**Note:** If your scraping application only needs standard `HTTP` or `HTTPS` (`TCP`) connections, use our main backconnect endpoint (`pr.oxylabs.io:7777`). MASQUE introduces `QUIC` connection setup overhead that is only necessary when you require `UDP` or native `HTTP/3` transport.
{% endhint %}

### MASQUE setup <a href="#masque-setup" id="masque-setup"></a>

**For full setup, configuration, authentication details, see the technical setup guide below.**

<details>

<summary><strong>MASQUE Setup &#x26; Configuration</strong></summary>

<table data-header-hidden><thead><tr><th width="164"></th><th width="218"></th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Proxy endpoint</strong></td><td><code>masque.oxylabs.io:50000</code></td><td>Dedicated QUIC entry node</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Transport</strong></td><td><code>HTTP/3</code> over <code>QUIC</code></td><td>Uses UDP port <code>50000</code></td></tr><tr><td><strong>ALPN</strong></td><td><code>h3</code></td><td>Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation string</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Datagram support</strong></td><td><code>EnableDatagrams: true</code></td><td>Must be enabled in your client's QUIC setup</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Max datagram size</strong></td><td><code>1500</code> bytes</td><td>Datagrams exceeding 1500 bytes are dropped by the proxy</td></tr><tr><td><strong>TLS verification</strong></td><td>Standard Public CA</td><td>No custom CA certificates or overrides required</td></tr></tbody></table>

### Endpoint configuration & URI formats <a href="#endpoint-configuration-and-uri-formats" id="endpoint-configuration-and-uri-formats"></a>

To establish a tunnel, your client sends a `CONNECT` request with `:protocol = connect-udp` to the proxy listener:

* **RFC 9298 Standard (Recommended):** `https://masque.oxylabs.io:50000/.well-known/masque/udp/{target_host}/{target_port}/`
* **Legacy Query Format:** `https://masque.oxylabs.io:50000/masque?h={target_host}&p={target_port}`

**Hostnames & IPs:** The proxy resolves hostnames on your behalf through the residential exit node. You can pass domain names (`example.com`) or IP addresses (`1.2.3.4`). IPv6 addresses must be percent-encoded (e.g., `2001%3Adb8%3A%3A1`).

### Authentication <a href="#authentication" id="authentication"></a>

Authentication is handled via standard **HTTP Basic authentication** using the `Proxy-Authorization` header sent on the `CONNECT-UDP` request:

```bash
Proxy-Authorization: Basic Base64(customer-USERNAME[-key-value]:PASSWORD)
```

You use your standard Oxylabs proxy credentials. [Location settings](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings) and [session parameters](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/session-control) function identically to standard `HTTP/HTTPS` proxies. For example:

```bash
Proxy-Authorization: Basic customer-myuser-cc-us-sessid-abc123:PASSWORD
```

### Nested QUIC & packet size <a href="#nested-quic-and-packet-size" id="nested-quic-and-packet-size"></a>

When using HTTP/3 through MASQUE, a second QUIC stack runs over the proxy tunnel (*nested QUIC)*. The outer connection (*client-to-proxy*) wraps inner connection packets (*client-to-target*), adding *\~*&#x34;0 bytes of protocol framing overhead.

{% hint style="danger" %}
You must manually configure packet sizes and disable Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) on both client QUIC stacks. If skipped, the initial inner handshake packet will exceed outer datagram limits and be silently dropped by the proxy, causing the connection to hang indefinitely.
{% endhint %}

To set up your connection correctly, adjust the following:

1. **Disable PMTUD:** Turn off Path MTU Discovery on both outer and inner QUIC connections to enforce fixed packet limits.
2. **Outer QUIC (Client-to-Proxy):** Set initial/maximum packet size to `1392` bytes.
3. **Inner QUIC (Client-to-Target):** Set initial/maximum packet size to `1352` bytes.

{% hint style="info" %}
The \~40-byte difference supports outer QUIC headers, AEAD encryption tags, DATAGRAM frame headers, HTTP-datagram framing under RFC 9297, and CONNECT-UDP context IDs under RFC 9298.
{% endhint %}

### Response status codes <a href="#response-status-codes" id="response-status-codes"></a>

<table><thead><tr><th width="80">Code</th><th width="260">Status</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>200</code></td><td><code>OK</code></td><td>Tunnel established. UDP datagrams can now flow on the request stream.</td></tr><tr><td><code>400</code></td><td><code>Bad Request</code></td><td>Malformed target URI or invalid request parameters.</td></tr><tr><td><code>407</code></td><td><code>Proxy Authentication Required</code></td><td>Authentication failed or account traffic limit reached.</td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

## SOCKS5

Oxylabs Residential Proxies support `SOCKS5` connections over `TCP` and `UDP`.&#x20;

{% hint style="info" %}
SOCKS5 connection supports both `socks5h://` and `socks5://`:&#x20;

* `socks5h` passes the hostname
* `socks5` passes resolved IP
  {% endhint %}

For a standard `SOCKS5` connection, use `socks5h://` with your connection string:

```
socks5h://pr.oxylabs.io:7777
```

{% hint style="warning" %}

* `SOCKS5` proxy authentication is not supported by Google Chrome. Use Mozilla Firefox or HTTP clients instead.
* Certain target websites can identify proxy traffic using `SOCKS5`. If you encounter connection errors, switch to `HTTP` or `HTTPS`.
* `SOCKS5` connections do not support country-specific entry points (e.g. `de-pr.oxylabs.io`) and localization must be used through username-based [location parameters](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings).
* `Google` is a restricted target to use with `UDP` connection.
  {% endhint %}

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```bash
curl -x socks5h://pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-cc-FR:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import requests

proxies = {
    'http': 'socks5h://customer-USERNAME-cc-FR:PASSWORD@pr.oxylabs.io:7777',
    'https': 'socks5h://customer-USERNAME-cc-FR:PASSWORD@pr.oxylabs.io:7777'
}

response = requests.get('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location', proxies=proxies)
print(response.text)
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$country = 'FR';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';

$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "socks5h://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-cc-$country:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

## Allowed proxy target ports

The default configuration of proxy ports includes `80` and `443`, designed to accommodate standard `HTTP` and `HTTPS` protocols. `HTTP/3 (MASQUE)` operates on UDP port `50000`.&#x20;

| Protocol          | Transport | Port    |
| ----------------- | --------- | ------- |
| `HTTP`            | TCP       | `80`    |
| `HTTPS`           | TCP       | `443`   |
| `HTTP/3 (MASQUE)` | UDP       | `50000` |

To access other ports, it is necessary to undergo compliance verification, please contact our [**support**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io).


# Advanced Filters

Learn how to filter Residential Proxies by operating system (OS) or IP version using advanced parameters.

Oxylabs Residential Proxies support advanced filtering parameters to adjust your proxy pool by **Operating System (OS)** platform fingerprint or **IP protocol version (IPv4 vs. IPv6)**.

{% hint style="success" %}
**To enable this feature**, contact your Account Manager (details available in the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/)). You may need to complete a quick [KYC](https://oxylabs.io/kyc-and-safety) procedure.
{% endhint %}

<table><thead><tr><th width="117">Filter</th><th width="106">Parameter</th><th width="221">Values</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="#platform-os-filtering"><strong>Platform (OS)</strong></a></td><td><code>platform</code></td><td><code>windows</code>, <code>macos</code>, <code>linux</code>, <code>android</code>, <code>ios</code></td><td>Matches TCP connection fingerprint to target OS.</td></tr><tr><td><a href="#ip-version-selection-ipv4-ipv6"><strong>IP Version</strong></a></td><td><code>ipversion</code></td><td><code>ipversion-4</code>, <code>ipversion-6</code></td><td>Restricts proxy pool strictly to IPv4 or IPv6.</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Platform (OS)

The `platform` parameter matches the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) fingerprint of the residential proxy exit node to a specified operating system. Matching your proxy's OS fingerprint with your client HTTP headers (e.g., emulating Chrome on Windows) prevents fingerprint mismatches that target websites use to detect bot traffic.

Supported `platform` values:

* `windows`
* `macos`
* `linux`
* `android`
* `ios`

```
customer-USERNAME-platform-windows:PASSWORD
```

{% hint style="warning" %}
**Note:** Because residential proxies are dynamic peer devices, pool availability may be constrained when combining `platform` with [location parameters](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings) (such as `city` or `postalcode`).&#x20;
{% endhint %}

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```bash
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-platform-windows:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import urllib.request

username = 'USERNAME'
password = 'PASSWORD'
entry = f'http://customer-{username}-platform-windows:{password}@pr.oxylabs.io:7777'

query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({'http': entry, 'https': entry})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read().decode('utf-8'))
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$platform = 'windows';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';

$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-platform-$platform:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

## IP version

By default, Oxylabs Residential Proxies use both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. To force connections exclusively through IPv4 or IPv6 exit nodes, pass the `ipversion` parameter with your username string as either `ipversion-4` (IPv4 pool) or `ipversion-6` (IPv6 pool):

```
customer-USERNAME-ipversion-X:PASSWORD
```

If you use `ipversion-6` on a target website that does not support IPv6, Oxylabs proxies automatically resolve the request via IPv4 by default to prevent connection failures.

{% hint style="info" %}
To disable automatic fallback and enforce strict IPv6 routing, contact your Account Manager. If strict routing is enabled and the target lacks IPv6 support, requests will return an HTTP `522 Bad Response` error.
{% endhint %}

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```bash
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-ipversion-6:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import urllib.request

username = 'USERNAME'
password = 'PASSWORD'
entry = f'http://customer-{username}-ipversion-6:{password}@pr.oxylabs.io:7777'

query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({'http': entry, 'https': entry})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read().decode('utf-8'))
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';

$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username-ipversion-6:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}


# IP Whitelisting & Auth

Learn how to create or edit an IP whitelist for your Residential Proxies.

IP whitelisting allows you to access Oxylabs Residential Proxies using your personal whitelisted IPs to bypass username and password requirement in your proxy request.

{% hint style="warning" %}
**Do not mix authentication methods.** If your source IP is whitelisted, connect using either IP authentication or credential authentication and never both simultaneously. Passing credentials from a whitelisted IP can cause unexpected routing behavior or browser `407 Proxy Authentication Required` errors.
{% endhint %}

## Create an IP whitelist

To enable IP-based authentication, register your server's static public IPv4 address in the Oxylabs Dashboard.

1. Log in to the [**Oxylabs Dashboard**](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/).
2. Create a Residential Proxy product instance.
3. In the **Authentication setting** select **Whitelisted IPs**.

   <figure><img src="https://3826932121-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FBQ7Zf9paoN3FTeGcyfY1%2Fuploads%2FQ2n1AyQHRvSd6CgAJsPE%2FScreenshot%202026-10-05%20at%2004.17.12.png?alt=media&amp;token=0799c543-bb9a-495e-a6b7-d842b6c19fa9" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>
4. Enter **up to 10 public IPv4** addresses (in `xx.xx.xx.xx` format).
5. Fill in all necessary details and click **Create instance**.

{% hint style="info" %}
**Note:** A single IP address can be whitelisted for only one Residential Proxies instance at a time. If the IP is already whitelisted on another instance, remove it from there before adding it to a new one.
{% endhint %}

{% hint style="warning" %}

* Make sure you are not connected to a VPN or local proxy service when checking your public IP address.
* If your team shares a public IP address or requires individual sub-user tracking, use credential authentication instead of IP whitelisting.
  {% endhint %}

## Requests with whitelisted IPs

When using IP Whitelisting, parameters (such as [location](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings), [session IDs](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/session-control), or ASNs) cannot be embedded into a username string. Instead, all proxy flags are added directly to the entry node host address as a subdomain pointing to `.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777`.

```
cc-us-city-new_york-sessid-test123.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777
```

<table><thead><tr><th width="149">Type</th><th width="119">Parameter</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#country"><strong>Country targeting</strong></a></td><td><code>cc</code></td><td>2-letter ISO country code.<br>E.g. <code>cc-de.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#city"><strong>City targeting</strong></a></td><td><code>city</code></td><td>Requires <code>cc</code> parameter. Spaces use <code>_</code>.<br>E.g. <code>cc-us-city-new_york.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#state"><strong>State targeting</strong></a></td><td><code>st</code></td><td>US states; requires <code>us_</code> prefix.<br>E.g. <code>st-us_california.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#continent"><strong>Continent targeting</strong></a></td><td><code>cn</code></td><td>2-letter continent code (<code>AF</code>, <code>AN</code>, <code>AS</code>, <code>EU</code>, <code>NA</code>, <code>OC</code>, <code>SA</code>).<br>E.g. <code>cn-eu.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#zip-postal-code"><strong>ZIP / Postal code targeting</strong></a></td><td><code>postalcode</code></td><td>5-digit US ZIP code; requires <code>cc-us</code>.<br>E.g. <code>cc-us-postalcode-90210.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#geo-hash"><strong>Geo hash targeting</strong></a></td><td><code>geohash</code></td><td>Grid cell levels 1 to 4 (<code>9</code> to <code>drq4</code>).<br>E.g. <code>geohash-u09.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#asn-targeting"><strong>ASN tageting</strong></a></td><td><code>ASN</code></td><td>Target specific Autonomous System Numbers.<br>E.g. <code>asn-21928.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/session-control#default-sticky-sessions-sessid"><strong>Sticky session</strong></a></td><td><code>sessid</code></td><td>Binds sequential requests to the same IP (10-min default).<br>E.g. <code>sessid-test123.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr><tr><td><a href="/products/proxies/residential-proxies/session-control#extend-session-duration-sesstime"><strong>Session duration</strong></a></td><td><code>sesstime</code></td><td>Extends session duration in minutes.<br>E.g. <code>sessid-test123-sesstime-15.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777</code></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### Code examples

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x https://cc-us-city-new_york-sessid-test123.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777 https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$session_id = 'test123';  // Your session ID
$city = 'new_york';  // The city you want to target
$proxy = "cc-us-city-$city-sessid-$session_id.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777";
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');

curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);

if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>

```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import urllib.request

session_id = 'test123'  # Your session ID
city = 'new_york'  # The city you want to target
proxy = 'cc-us-city-%s-sessid-%s.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777' % (city, session_id)

query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({
    'http': proxy,
    'https': proxy,
})

execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())

```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Java" %}

```java
package example;

import org.apache.http.HttpHost;
import org.apache.http.client.fluent.*;

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        HttpHost entry = new HttpHost("cc-us-city-new_york-sessid-test123.bc.pr.oxylabs.io", 7777);

        String query = Executor.newInstance()
            .execute(Request.Get("http://ip.oxylabs.io/location").viaProxy(entry))
            .returnContent().asString();
        
        System.out.println(query);
    }
}

```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="C#" %}

```csharp
using System;
using System.Net;

class Example
{
    static void Main()
    {
        var client = new WebClient();
        
        client.Proxy = new WebProxy("cc-us-city-new_york-sessid-test123.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777");

        Console.WriteLine(client.DownloadString("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location"));
    }
}

```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Go" %}

```ruby
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"io/ioutil"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
)

func main() {
	proxyURL, _ := url.Parse("https://cc-us-city-new_york-sessid-test123.bc.pr.oxylabs.io:7777")
	client := &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{Proxy: http.ProxyURL(proxyURL)}}

	resp, err := client.Get("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location")
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("Error:", err)
		return
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	body, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	fmt.Println(string(body))
}
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}


# Endpoint Generator

Simplify integration with the Endpoint Generator. Configure Residential Proxy locations, sessions, and authentication to export your lists.

The Endpoint Generator is an automated tool accessed via the [Oxylabs Dashboard](https://dashboard.oxylabs.io/?route=/overview/RP/endpoint-generator) and designed to generate custom lists of Residential Proxy endpoints. Endpoint generator can be found in your Residential Proxy product instance **Overview**:

<figure><img src="https://3826932121-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FBQ7Zf9paoN3FTeGcyfY1%2Fuploads%2FrHCBVyXaPFpP0V2ovcu5%2FScreenshot%202026-10-05%20at%2004.25.56.png?alt=media&amp;token=3fadc048-8e78-4638-81ed-ebdfeb532ce7" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>

It allows you to select location, session type, protocol format, and output options, then export ready-to-use proxy lists in CSV, JSON, or TXT formats.

### How to generate proxy endpoints

{% stepper %}
{% step %}

### Select proxy country

Choose the Residential proxy country and city. If left as `Any`, random location will be selected.

<figure><img src="https://3826932121-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FBQ7Zf9paoN3FTeGcyfY1%2Fuploads%2FvAG0awF8ahTSrfjXOjZH%2FScreenshot%202026-10-05%20at%2004.31.30.png?alt=media&amp;token=3c6d50f3-4ec5-4c4a-aeb4-0cce6f4ae941" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>

Check the [location settings](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings) page to learn more.
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Select region

Choose your connection region based on your client application's location:

* **Global:** Standard entry nodes for connections.
* **Hong Kong / Beijing:** Dedicated entry nodes optimized for connections from [China](/products/proxies/residential-proxies/location-settings#china-entry-nodes).

<figure><img src="https://3826932121-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FBQ7Zf9paoN3FTeGcyfY1%2Fuploads%2FAh72IEamytZyFMXt4cjm%2FScreenshot%202026-10-05%20at%2004.27.29.png?alt=media&amp;token=f8cc197e-811c-444f-a982-82a7cd672487" alt="" width="375"><figcaption></figcaption></figure>
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Set proxy protocol

Choose from available proxy protocols:

* **HTTP:** `http://pr.oxylabs.io:7777`
* **HTTPS:** `https://pr.oxylabs.io:7777`
* **SOCKS5:** `socks5h://pr.oxylabs.io:7777`
  {% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Select session type

* ​[**Sticky session**](https://app.gitbook.com/o/YFRJGnXcbhIMTe1cuCmz/sites/site_rPdpB/s/BQ7Zf9paoN3FTeGcyfY1/proxies/residential-proxies/session-control)**:** Allows you to keep the same IP address for a specified duration (max 1440 minutes).
* **Rotating session:** Receive a new IP address with each request.
* [**Sticky session (one-IP)**](#single-ip-strict-session-binding-sessid_oneip)**:** Binds strictly to a single exit node. Fails with HTTP `502` if IP drops.
  {% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Set duration (Sticky session)

Choose the session duration on the slider for your sticky session between `1` minute and `1440` minutes (default – `10`).
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Select output format

Choose the output format from:

* cURL
* Python
* PHP
* Node.js
* GO
* Java
* Integrations

<figure><img src="https://3826932121-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FBQ7Zf9paoN3FTeGcyfY1%2Fuploads%2Fm08UmoUrS3FzVextbTHO%2FScreenshot%202026-10-05%20at%2004.46.04.png?alt=media&amp;token=2c262214-27f4-4cf1-ae28-a2e2d33e5751" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

That's it! You have successfully created a ready-to-use list of Residential Proxies endpoints!


# Restricted Targets

Find out which targets are restricted when using our Residential Proxies.

Some websites are restricted on our Residential Proxy network to avoid abuse and suspicious activities.

{% hint style="success" %}
**Some targets can be enabled after going through a short KYC procedure.** Get in touch with our [**Customer Support Team**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) if your target falls under the mentioned groups to ensure you can access the target before purchasing.
{% endhint %}

**❗️The list includes but is not limited to targets such as:**

| Target category                          | Example                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Entertainment & streaming                | Netflix, Spotify, Twitch, Disney |
| Banking and other financial institutions | PayPal, Bank of America, Binance |
| Government websites                      | usa.gov, canada.ca               |
| Gaming                                   | Playstation, Steam               |
| Ticketing                                | Ticketmaster, Eventbrite         |
| Mailing                                  | Outlook, Yahoo mail              |
| Ads                                      | Google Tag Manager, Doubleclick  |
| IP checking websites\*                   | ipinfo.info, 2ip.io              |

{% hint style="success" %}
\* Please use `ip.oxylabs.io ip.oxylabs.io/json` or `ip.oxylabs.io/location` to check your IP address.
{% endhint %}

Get in touch with our customer support team at [**support@oxylabs.io**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) or via the 24/7 live chat on our [**website**](https://oxylabs.io/).


# Response Codes

Learn about different response codes for Residential Proxies. Understand issues under the codes and resolve common status errors.

When an error originates within the Oxylabs proxy infrastructure, the response includes an `X-Error-Description` **HTTP header** explaining the root cause and recommended action.

{% hint style="warning" %}
If an error originates directly from the target website (e.g., target-side `404` or `403` codes), the `X-Error-Description` header will not be present. Inspect your request headers, TLS fingerprint, or retry logic when debugging target-side errors.
{% endhint %}

<table><thead><tr><th width="119.86328125">Response Code</th><th width="198">Error Message</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>200</code></td><td><code>OK</code></td><td>Tunnel established successfully.</td></tr><tr><td rowspan="4"><code>400</code></td><td rowspan="4"><code>Bad Request</code></td><td>Could not parse the request. Please check if the request is formatted correctly.</td></tr><tr><td>SOCKS version unsupported. Please use SOCKS5 to make requests.</td></tr><tr><td>Unsupported parameters were used. Please contact support or your account manager if you have any questions.</td></tr><tr><td>Invalid HTTP request received. Please try again.</td></tr><tr><td><code>403</code></td><td><code>Access Denied</code></td><td>Restricted target. Please contact support or your account manager if you have any questions.</td></tr><tr><td rowspan="2"><code>407</code></td><td rowspan="2"><code>Access Denied</code></td><td>User authentication failed. Please check your credentials and try again.</td></tr><tr><td>Traffic limit reached. Please contact support or your account manager if you have any questions.</td></tr><tr><td><code>500</code></td><td><code>Internal Server Error</code></td><td>We have encountered an internal error. Please try again.</td></tr><tr><td rowspan="6"><code>502</code></td><td rowspan="2"><code>Bad Response</code></td><td>Invalid HTTP response received during the request. Please try again.</td></tr><tr><td>Invalid response received during the request. Please try again.</td></tr><tr><td rowspan="4"><code>Bad Gateway</code></td><td>Session failed. Please start a new session.</td></tr><tr><td>Exit node not found (session ended). Try using different filters (or start a new session).</td></tr><tr><td>We have encountered an error. Please try again.</td></tr><tr><td>Client disconnected. Please try again.</td></tr><tr><td rowspan="2"><code>504</code></td><td rowspan="2"><code>Timeout</code></td><td>Request timed out. Please try again.</td></tr><tr><td>Unable to reach the target. Please check if the target URL is correct and try again.</td></tr><tr><td><code>522</code></td><td><code>Bad Response</code></td><td>Invalid response received during the request. Please try again.</td></tr></tbody></table>

If you encounter a response code that's not listed here, please reach out to [**Customer Support**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) or your Account Manager for further assistance.


# Public API

Programmatically manage Residential Proxy sub-users, set traffic limits, and track usage statistics with the Public API.

The [**Public API**](https://residential-api.oxylabs.io/v2/docs) allows you to **manage proxy users programmatically** (via RESTful interface `https://residential-api.oxylabs.io/v2`) without using the dashboard. You can create, delete, and modify proxy sub-users, set traffic usage limits, and view current and historic traffic usage.

### Available API paths

Base Endpoint:

```
https://residential-api.oxylabs.io/v2
```

<table data-full-width="false"><thead><tr><th width="78.15625">Method</th><th width="406.92578125">Path</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><mark style="color:$success;">POST</mark></td><td><code>/login</code></td><td>Authenticate to get the access token (JWT).</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="color:blue;">GET</mark></td><td><code>/users/{userId}/sub-users</code></td><td>Retrieve all active sub-users</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="color:$success;">POST</mark></td><td><code>/users/{userId}/sub-users</code></td><td>Create a new sub-user.</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="color:blue;">GET</mark></td><td><code>/users/{userId}/sub-users/{subUserId}</code></td><td>Retrieve traffic usage statistics for a specific sub-user.</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="color:$primary;">PATCH</mark></td><td><code>/users/{userId}/sub-users/{subUserId}</code></td><td>Modify a sub-user.</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="color:red;">DELETE</mark></td><td><code>/users/{userId}/sub-users/{subUserId}</code></td><td>Delete a sub-user.</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="color:blue;">GET</mark></td><td><code>/users/{userId}/sub-users/{subUserId}/target-stats</code></td><td>Get sub-user traffic usage per target domain (last 30 days, requires specific date).</td></tr><tr><td><mark style="color:blue;">GET</mark></td><td><code>/users/{userId}/client-stats</code></td><td>Retrieve total traffic usage for the current month.</td></tr></tbody></table>

### Authentication & usage flow

All API requests (except `/login`) require a JSON Web Token (JWT) passed in the `Authorization: Bearer {token}` HTTP header.

{% hint style="info" %}
The `login` endpoint requires your Main User credentials (the first sub-user in your dashboard users list). If you recently changed your main user password, use the original password or [contact support](mailto:support@oxylabs.io).&#x20;
{% endhint %}

{% hint style="warning" %}
The generated JWT access token expires in 1 hour. After expiration, you must request a new token via `POST /login`.
{% endhint %}

{% stepper %}
{% step %}

### Generate JWT access token

Authenticate via `POST /login` using HTTP Basic Authentication with your main user credentials (encoded in base64).

```bash
curl -X "POST" \
  "https://residential-api.oxylabs.io/v2/login" \
  -H "accept: application/json" \
  -u "MAIN_USERNAME:MAIN_PASSWORD"
```

The response includes two key values:

```json
{
  "user_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}
```

Save the returned `user_id` and `token` for all subsequent requests.
{% endstep %}

{% step %}

### Make authenticated API requests

Include the JWT in the `Authorization: Bearer {token}` header and pass your `user_id` in the request path to query the API to manage users and check statistics.

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```bash
curl -X "GET" \
  "https://residential-api.oxylabs.io/v2/users/YOUR_USER_ID/client-stats" \
  -H "accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import requests

user_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
jwt_token = "YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"

url = f"https://residential-api.oxylabs.io/v2/users/{user_id}/client-stats"
headers = {
    "accept": "application/json",
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {jwt_token}"
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.json())
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Node.js" %}

```javascript
const axios = require('axios');

const userId = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000';
const jwtToken = 'YOUR_JWT_TOKEN';

axios.get(`https://residential-api.oxylabs.io/v2/users/${userId}/client-stats`, {
  headers: {
    'accept': 'application/json',
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${jwtToken}`
  }
})
.then(response => console.log(response.data))
.catch(error => console.error(error));
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

#### Output sample

```json
{
  "traffic": 1.2354839,
  "date_from": "2026-09-01",
  "date_to": "2026-09-14"
}
```

{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

### Backconnect entry setup (CNAME)

To route proxy traffic through your custom domain name instead of `pr.oxylabs.io`, configure a DNS `CNAME` record in your DNS provider manager.

1. Create a new `CNAME` record in your DNS provider (e.g., Cloudflare, Route 53).
2. Set the hostname/subdomain (e.g., `entry.yourdomain.com`) to target `pr.oxylabs.io`.
3. Use your custom domain name in place of `pr.oxylabs.io` across all proxy request connection strings.

![Backconnect](https://3826932121-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FBQ7Zf9paoN3FTeGcyfY1%2Fuploads%2Fgit-blob-9d15ff608e52a76e6d288eb45c3bd648ddf970ef%2Fcname.jpg?alt=media)

For more information, please contact [**Customer support**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io) or your account manager.


# Mobile Proxies

Real mobile proxy IPs from 140+ locations with automatic rotation. Thie documentation covers setup, session control, protocols, Public API integration, and more.

[**Mobile Proxies**](https://oxylabs.io/products/mobile-proxies) contain real IP addresses provided by Internet Service Providers (ISPs). These IP addresses are attached to mobile devices across the globe at a country level. Therefore, it is easy to replicate human behaviour and avoid blocks using this type of proxy.

Oxylabs Mobile Proxies are fully equipped, rotate automatically, and are easy to set up. Mobile Proxies allow you to access 3G/4G/5G cellular networks.

Find everything about Mobile Proxies integration in this documentation, and to begin with, check the **Getting started** section below.

## Getting started

Make a request to `https://ip.oxylabs.io/location` using a mobile proxy from a random location through our [**backconnect entry**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/making-requests). Replace `USERNAME` and `PASSWORD` with your proxy user credentials. Keep in mind that each request returns a new IP address as Oxylabs Mobile Proxies rotate automatically.

{% hint style="info" %}
Use [**ip.oxylabs.io/location**](https://ip.oxylabs.io/location) to check the parameters of your IPs—this domain delivers information from four geolocation databases: MaxMind, IP2Location, DB-IP, and IPinfo.io. The parameters include IP address, provider, country, city, ZIP code, ASN, organization name, time zone, and meta (when disclosed by database).
{% endhint %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% hint style="info" %}
Our Mobile Proxies support `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, `HTTP3`, and `SOCKS5` protocols. You can learn more about using them [**here**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/protocols).
{% endhint %}

Now make a request using a proxy from France. All you need to do is add `cc-FR` to your username string. Below is an example in cURL, and [**here**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/location-settings/country) you can find code samples in other languages.

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-cc-FR:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

If you need to keep the same proxy for more than one request, use [**session control**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/session-control)**.** Add `sessid-abc12345` to your username string, where `abc12345` can be any random string, and as long as you keep sending requests with this string (session ID), you will get the same proxy IP.

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME-sessid-randomString123:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

You can also set up Mobile Proxies using the [**Endpoint generator**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/endpoint-generator).

If you have any additional questions, please contact your account manager or our support team at [**support@oxylabs.io**](mailto:support@oxylabs.io).


# Making Requests

Learn to make requests with Oxylabs Mobile Proxies. Master the basic query structure and use parameters for location targeting, city selection, and sessions.

## Basic query

Basic query only requires passing `username` and `password`. No other parameters are needed. Such a query will result in the request being made from a random IP address (proxy). Every new request will use a different proxy.

### Code examples

In this example, a query to `ip.oxylabs.io` is performed from a random IP:

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="cURL" %}

```shell
curl -x pr.oxylabs.io:7777 -U "customer-USERNAME:PASSWORD" https://ip.oxylabs.io/location
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="PHP" %}

```php
<?php
$username = 'USERNAME';
$password = 'PASSWORD';
$proxy = 'pr.oxylabs.io:7777';
$query = curl_init('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location');
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, 1);
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXY, "http://$proxy");
curl_setopt($query, CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, "customer-$username:$password");
$output = curl_exec($query);
curl_close($query);
if ($output)
    echo $output;
?>
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Python" %}

```python
import urllib.request
import random
username = 'USERNAME'
password = 'PASSWORD'
entry = ('http://customer-%s:%s@pr.oxylabs.io:7777' %
    (username, password))
query = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({
    'http': entry,
    'https': entry,
})
execute = urllib.request.build_opener(query)
print(execute.open('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location').read())
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Java" %}

```java
package example;

import org.apache.http.HttpHost;
import org.apache.http.client.fluent.*;

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        HttpHost entry = new HttpHost("pr.oxylabs.io", 7777);
        String query = Executor.newInstance()
            .auth(entry, "customer-USERNAME", "PASS")
            .execute(Request.Get("http://ip.oxylabs.io/location").viaProxy(entry))
            .returnContent().asString();
        System.out.println(query);
    }
}
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="C#" %}

```csharp
using System;
using System.Net;

class Example
{
    static void Main()
    {
        var client = new WebClient();
        client.Proxy = new WebProxy("pr.oxylabs.io:7777");
        client.Proxy.Credentials = new NetworkCredential("customer-USERNAME", "PASSWORD");
        Console.WriteLine(client.DownloadString("https://ip.oxylabs.io/location"));
    }
c
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Ruby" %}

```ruby
require 'uri'
require 'net/http'

uri = URI.parse('https://ip.oxylabs.io/location')
proxy = Net::HTTP::Proxy('pr.oxylabs.io', 7777, 'customer-USERNAME', 'PASSWORD')

req = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri.path)

result = proxy.start(uri.host,uri.port) do |http|
    http.request(req)
end

puts result.body
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

A single backconnect proxy enables you to choose a specific country proxy via additional parameters in the username. This approach also supports session control. Below is a sample of credentials structure:

`customer-USERNAME-cc-US-sessid-abcde12345:PASSWORD`

### Query parameters

| Parameter                                                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <mark style="background-color:green;">**customer**</mark> | Username                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `cc`                                                      | Case insensitive country code in 2-letter [**3166-1 alpha-2 format**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2). For example, `DE` for Germany, `GB` for the United Kingdom, `TH` for Thailand. You can find more details on how to use country-specific proxies [**here**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/location-settings/country#country-specific-entry-nodes).                                                                                        |
| `city`                                                    | Case insensitive city name in English. This parameter must be accompanied by `cc` for better accuracy, for example, `cc-GB-city-london` for London, United Kingdom; `cc-DE-city-berlin` for Berlin, Germany. For a city with more than two words, replace space with `_`, for example, `city-st_petersburg` or `city-rio_de_janeiro`. Click [**here**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/location-settings/select-city) for more information on city-level targeting. |
| `st`                                                      | Case insensitive US state name with us\_ in the beginning, for example, `us_california`, `us_illinois`. [**Click here**](/products/proxies/mobile-proxies/location-settings/select-state) for more information on state-level targeting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `sessid`                                                  | Session ID to keep the same IP with upcoming queries. The session expires in 10 minutes. After that, a new IP address is assigned to that session ID. Random string, 0-9, and A-Z characters are supported.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `sesstime`                                                | The session time parameter keeps the same IP for a certain period. The maximum session time is 30 minutes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| <mark style="background-color:green;">**password**</mark> | Password                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

\- Mandatory parameter

## Entry nodes for China

We have configured entry nodes in Hong Kong and Beijing regions for better connectivity from China. Note that it is an HTTPS proxy node. All username parameters are identical to the regular entry node.

We are currently working on fixing the rest of the integrations on which HTTPS protocol will be supported.

```
https://a81298871.com:8000 - Hong Kong
```
